entry.title: Research Proposal 怎么写？ 你的潜在导师们究竟想看到什么？
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @coldsake_（Linote 🎃🍷🥃🍸🍹🍶） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

写Research Proposal (RP) 给潜在导师，就像做生意

首先需要明白的是你的导师（客户）是什么人

1.三种导师：

A. 在一线的导师：他们明白什么是行业最前沿的东西

B. 不在一线的导师：他们明白行业次前沿的东西

C. 想偷你idea的导师：他们想偷你idea，他们很push，也会各种挑刺。

2.RP 该写什么：

A和B 往往是很清楚一个 申请的学生 对整个行业的熟悉程度 也很清楚学生能写出什么样的RP。

凭借 本科+硕士 的经历 是几乎不可能写出 beyond current 的 RP的。

所以该写什么？ —— Topic + Methodology + Contribution

简单说就是：用什么方法解决什么问题，带来什么贡献。

Topic 不要是Hot 的 但是要是 New 的。

Methodology 要是Genenral or Classic，不是非常 新的。

Contribution 就是画饼了，说你的这个研究能有什么贡献，能带来什么影响

2.1 什么是Hot Topic 和 New Topic

在此之前，我们要洞悉一个topic的生命周期。

假设一个Topic 从2016年开始有人提起，大概2022年 进入Hot的状态，但是取决于发表篇数，一般年发表超5~10篇就算Hot；次年一定会有许多人去申请Funding，此时把这个topic 作为你的RP 就不合适，因为和你topic 类似的申请者一定很多，同质化一定很强。

至于一年20篇等的，说明其他人在上一年，甚至是前两年拿到了funding了，在进入产出的阶段，这个周期一定会有其他领域的人，想来做交叉。申请funding的时候同质化会更强、也会更紧张。

所以Hot topic 是一定不适合作为RP的topic的。

那么New topic，就是这个课题只被提过一两次/年，一年发表大概在一篇左右。又或者没有人提过，但是在其他行业已经被吃透了。

那么它就适合拿来做你的RP topic，会相对的新，你的意向导师也会对此满意。

认为你的想法和主见很好。Funding 也相对好申请。

2.2 Methodology 怎么选

选择领域里面常用的，经典的。

搞清楚 你是来解决问题的，不是来推陈出新的。

一定一定不要在PhD阶段去开发方法，即便这个新方法很新 一定能成。

它也会耗费你至少两年的时间。发表也会变得困难

2.3 Contribution 怎么写

学术界的贡献本身是一种表演行为。营销你的课题。

你不要管它真的做出了什么贡献，而是它能蹭上什么宏大叙事、什么可持续的叙事？

如果你不能营销的自己都信了，基金评委凭什么信你？

3. 避雷

1.没有一年或半年的 看文献，几乎很难写出 beyond current 的RP，所以申请的时候，身为导师，不会提这么过分的要求。

2.导师应该是会更你一起探讨RP该怎么写，然后给你提意见，给你大致方向的。

3.如果写RP的时候和导师沟通起来不舒服就赶紧跑，现在已经让你不适了，以后一定会更糟糕。

欢迎关注我，我是 Linote ，专注于 AI+学术 内容创作和分享。

entry.title: Monitor your CI performance using Sentry
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @sentry（Sentry） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

We use GitHub workflows to make sure our products match our expected quality standards, and by using Sentry Tracing we improved CI run time by 71%. Here’s how you can too:

Your workflows are slowing you down

Writing code and delivering new features is now faster than ever, especially when agents do the work. On the other hand, the build and verification processes become the new bottlenecks of engineering.

While the exact setup varies for each developer and project, a standard setup is automated testing in Continuous Integration (CI) pipelines, such as GitHub Actions. With the demand for quality assurance increasing, and feedback cycles taking longer because of slow or failed CI checks, the speed of delivering features slows down.

So you start to investigate what exactly is slowing you down.

GitHub provides insights into how long your jobs and workflows take in total, but it only surfaces combined run information at any given time, or a sum of all your run minutes. While this is helpful, it does not tell the full story when e.g. the same job takes 9 minutes on one run and 15 minutes on another. Besides that, you also have to actively monitor your run times to make sure they are stable (no flaky tests), and do not increase constantly until all your efforts are wasted.

So (if you have the bandwidth) you start to compare multiple runs, structure the data, extract trends manually, and see yourself become a data scientist instead of just delivering the features you initially wanted to.

Sentry’s distributed tracing can do that work for us: it treats a CI run like any other API request.

Investigating CI using Sentry Tracing

Each workflow consists of multiple jobs, with each job being a series of sequential steps, each with a different time duration. Using the model behind tracing, these steps can be represented as spans, with full workflows being shown as entire traces, leveraging many features of Sentry such as Explore and custom dashboards.

The following screenshot is an example trace of the .NET (macos) job in the build workflow of the Sentry .NET SDK. By opening it up in the trace explorer we can see that the step Build is the longest contributor with ~44 min of the overall ~1 h 23 min.

While the actual efforts that can improve workflow duration depend on your type of project and setup, in our case we were able to implement general improvement strategies such as proper caching strategies across runs and parallelizing tests.

Bringing it all together we can now open up another trace of the same workflow and see that the Build span is now down to only ~8 minutes, with an overall time of only ~24 min.

That makes this job about 3.4x faster, a 71% cut in duration.

Gaining visibility using custom dashboards

Using a custom dashboard we can now use the collected individual traces and compare the data across multiple jobs, allowing us to easily see p50 and p90 distributions over time, making sure we are not comparing outliers.

This shows us that efforts can really pay off as we are now able to say that we reduced the time of workflow runs by about 64%, allowing us to focus time on the right places.

Together with the new Sentry CLI we can go another step further and even access the raw data and use it to generate graphs making the gains even more accessible. Bringing it all together we can clearly see the downwards trend as expected:

The best part: you can use it too!

Collecting traces for GitHub Actions workflows is almost effortless. To get started all you need to do is follow these steps:

  1. Create a new project in Sentry, e.g. ci-telemetry or github-actions-ci-data. No worries about picking a platform or alerts for now, as it doesn’t matter for this use case.
  2. Next, create a private repository named .sentry in the GitHub organization or user account that owns the repositories you want to monitor. Each owner needs its own .sentry repository.
  3. In the new repository commit a file called sentry_config.ini and configure the DSN to the project you created earlier:[sentry-github-actions-app]
    dsn = https://@.ingest.sentry.io/
  4. Finally, install our GitHub App and make sure it can access .sentry and all the workflows you want to monitor in Sentry. Note: our GitHub App can’t read your code. It asks for read access to Actions, repository metadata and the single sentry_config.ini file. When a workflow job completes, the app looks up the run’s branch, commit and commit author (whose name and email become the event’s user), reads your DSN from .sentry, and sends the job to your Sentry project. Feel free to check out the code in the sentry-github-actions-app repository.

That’s it! One project, one repo, one commit and one app installation and you will start to receive GitHub workflow jobs as Sentry traces*.

  • Keep in mind that the ingested traces count toward your span quota (or your transaction quota on older plans).

Next steps for us at Sentry

The GitHub app to collect GitHub Actions workflow telemetry in Sentry should be considered experimental, but now it’s your time to shine!

Try it out and let us know what works for you, what can be improved, and what you want to see next. The easiest way to make your voice heard is upvoting and commenting on issues in the sentry-github-actions-app repo on GitHub.

entry.title: Building an Autonomous Inference System
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @lrzneedresearch（Lorenzo Xiao） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Since we started Inferact, I have been getting a lot of questions about how it relates to vLLM: what stays in the open-source project, who maintains it, and what Inferact is for. All great questions; I want to lay out how we think about our technical north star.

The short version is that Inferact builds an autonomous inference system around vLLM, that vLLM stays open, and every engine optimization we and the system build improves vLLM for the whole community.

Inference is the problem

Inference is the only problem we are solving.

Every week a lab ships a new model architecture, a chip vendor designs hardware with no tuned kernels, or a customer’s traffic shifts from short chat to long-context agents, and each novel combination needs its own tuning before it runs well. Models, hardware, and workloads each moves on their own pace, and the gap between them costs a lot: an unoptimized stack loses throughput and reliability.

vLLM’s job is to bridge this gap. But we realized, you can’t brute force a combinatorial explosion; a search space that’s 5000+ model, 1000+ chip architecture, and an infinitude of workloads.

Inferact is a center of gravity for best inference engineers in the world, many of them are the people who built vLLM. We are unified around one goal: build a system that improves the engine, and improves itself—full autonomy.

Our answer: An Autonomous Inference System around vLLM

At Inferact, we are building an autonomous inference system (AIS) around vLLM. Autonomous means it operates on its own: it takes a goal, works toward it, and seeks feedback, without anyone telling it exactly what to do next.

In practice, the system:

  • Sees the production workloads it operates or is authorized to observe, and learns from what the community shares, without needing access to their deployments.
  • Adapts to new models and new hardware, and to customer workloads as they shift.
  • Evolves its own code and its own brain, the accumulated knowledge and engineering taste behind every decision.
  • Drives itself toward its goals, working through roadblocks the way a strong engineering organization would.
  • Optimizes continuously against each workload’s own targets.

The point is extreme optimization for each point on the continuum of use cases our users and customers care about, on a reliable core that keeps getting better. We want the system’s evolution to be bound only by compute, up to the hardware’s speed of light.

What autonomous inference means in practice

Here is what it could look like on an ordinary day.

  • **3am. **A lab shares the preview of a new open model, and the system starts profiling it before anyone at Inferact is awake. Its novel attention variant has no tuned kernel, so it falls back to a generic path and misses the latency target.
  • 4am. Unprompted, the system starts a Hillclimb round: some agents write a megakernel for the variant, others fuse the new ops around existing kernels, and one rewrites an engine from scratch.
  • Overnight. Several candidates win in isolation and lose end to end. Only the combination that survives full serving benchmarks moves forward.
  • Morning. That combination is live at each customer’s workload requirements and chip architectures, and the winning changes land upstream in vLLM.
  • Evening. The system reviews its own day, notices that most of the failed candidates died at the same end-to-end gate, and rewrites its agents to run that check first.
  • Tomorrow. It keeps improving itself autonomously.

This flow depends on our production and open source flywheel:

Production. Writing a standalone engine and optimization is easy because inference tasks are generally verifiable. But this isolated gain typically falls short on production distribution and cannot be robust enough. vLLM runs production but it relies on the distributed inference stack to scale out. In order to verify the performance gain, only the engine that stands the test of prod traffic can be trusted.

Open source. vLLM is the land where optimization compounds. We carefully designed the core engine to be composable with many different optimizations. This allows every user to benefit from each release. The autonomous inference system benefits directly from the vast community and ecosystem of contributors, academic labs, and partners. I believe vLLM has access to the widest knowledge base of inference demand in the world; and we will enable the autonomous system to help us govern the project by triage issues and test pull requests faster.

Inferact exists to run this loop and to bring vLLM to production. That has three components.

  1. vLLM leads in the open, and we keep optimizing it. Every performance improvement we find goes upstream to vLLM.
  2. Inferact builds the autonomous system around vLLM. The goal is a system that maintains the inference engine and tailors it to each workload.
  3. Humans set the goals. Fundamentally, both of these require human taste to supply the quality bar and the ideas that improve the system.

Inferact only wins if vLLM keeps getting better for everyone.

Autonomous inference in production today

Parts of this loop already run in production at Inferact. Here are two examples.

**MiniMax M3.1 Flash. **M3.1 arrived with a new architecture: sparse attention with an indexer, a large MoE, vision input, and native DSpark speculative decoding. vLLM needed to run M3.1 on both NVIDIA and AMD at optimized performance from day 0, in production serving, and the workload kept changing shape underneath us, from long-context agentic coding to short-input, long-output traffic, and then to decode-bound serving once the final checkpoint doubled output length.

We ran open source and production on one branch, shadowed 100% of live M3 traffic onto M3.1 before cutover, and ran a production hillclimb against that traffic, promoting changes from local gates to online shadow evals.

Improvements to the production deployment, each upstreamed to vLLM as it landed:

  • p50 time to first token went from 1.5 seconds on the first non-PD endpoint to 0.8 seconds in production.
  • Patches to the expert-parallel prefill path cut TTFT by 60 to 70 percent.
  • Pipeline-parallel prefill delivered 19 to 46 percent more throughput than tensor parallel.
  • Output per AMD card improves 56%.

The missing kernels, including MSA attention, the indexer, and NVFP4 MoE, went upstream, and day-0 images shipped for NVIDIA and AMD.

Agent V on Kimi K3.1. Agent V is our shared agent infrastructure. Ask it in Slack and it completes the task in our sandbox with native support hillclimbing.

When we brought Kimi K3.1 up on our own serving stack, output quality degraded on certain batches. A 16-agent hillclimb on Agent V reproduced the problem, root-caused it to an attention routing switch that depended on batch composition, and shipped the fix.

  • K3.1 quality: the fix raised our DeepSWE score from 0.558 to 0.602, matching the model’s reference accuracy.
  • K3.1 prefill: a 24-hour hillclimb made time to first token 2.78x faster at 800k context on GB300.
  • K3.1 decode: a 30-hour hillclimb cut p99 time per output token by 35%.
  • K3 in production on GB300: throughput per GPU went from about 0.77M to 1.4M tokens per minute, roughly 1.8x, between mid-September and the end of October, through production hillclimbing.

Agent V runs mostly on Kimi K3 itself, served by vLLM: about 79 percent of its organic sessions and 53 percent of all its tokens come from our own open-weight deployment. More on Agent V later this week.

Where we go next

AIS is a north star. We haven’t got there yet; but we will keep building towards the full loop.

For now, compute is scarce; we can’t yet simulate the world well enough to test changes against traffic that never happened, which is also what Agent V would need to rewrite itself safely; and our feedback loop is still narrow, coming only from the deployments we operate and what customers and the community share.

However, we will aim to close that loop.

  • build one-click observability for vLLM so the system sees more of the world.
  • build an Agent V that works across partners and the vLLM community, so the whole ecosystem feeds it.
  • build this system that sees workloads, adapts to models chips, and improves itself without waiting on us.

The journey towards fully autonomous inference systems will be hard, we are fortunate to work with the best engineers and the entire inference community in the planet to achieve it. We will build the full loop end to end, crude as it is, expecting to fail and learn from it many times over.

entry.title: Nvidia Q3 Earnings Report: Reading Between the Lines
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @blocmates（blocmates.） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Nvidia just dropped its Q3 report. Unfortunately, there are no more affairs to report about, but there are some fascinating details in there that we promise are worth your attention.

Let’s jump right in.

The headlines:

  • Revenue has jumped from $96.2 billion in Q2 to $115.8 billion in Q3. A big 20% jump
  • Data centers now account for 93% of Nvidia’s revenue. That’s $107.6 billion coming in from their data center business
  • Shareholder returns: $28.1 billion through buybacks and dividends
  • Remaining buyback authorization: $227.3 billion
  • Operating income: $77.5 billion, up 115% YoY
  • Gross margin is under pressure. Reported at 74.8% for Q3 (down 0.2% QoQ) and expected to drop to 71-72% in Q4

Beyond the headline numbers, there are two important takeaways from the Q3 financials.

Pivot to infrastructure

As the revenue suggests, Nvidia is transitioning from simply a GPU company to a full-stack AI infrastructure company.

The company’s future is increasingly tied to:

  • Hyperscaler capital expenditure
  • Enterprise AI adoption
  • Inference demand
  • AI agent deployment
  • Sovereign AI infrastructure

This pivot is also clear with some of the partnerships announced in the report:

  • Vera CPUs: custom CPUs for AI infrastructure.
  • NVLink Fusion: connecting NVIDIA infrastructure to custom XPUs.
  • Spectrum-X: networking infrastructure.
  • BlueField-4: data processing and infrastructure security.
  • DSX POD: complete AI factory reference designs.
  • OpenShell: infrastructure for AI agent execution and security.

On top of this, Nvidia’s cloud service agreement and data center lease commitments have increased from $74 billion to $102 billion, further emphasizing the commitment to being at the heart of the physical infrastructure of AI.

The CFO’s commentary also disclosed a $105 billion guarantee connected to a huge OpenAI infrastructure development in Ohio.

The $390 billion bet on memory

AI GPUs are heavily dependent on high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which is expensive and difficult to manufacture at scale.

At the same time, Nvidia has some massive projects that are just beginning, like Blackwell and Vera Rubin.

So Nvidia has invested $390 billion in a multi-year procurement commitment for this memory to ensure it stays ahead of the pack.

The main risk here is simply a decrease in demand for AI infrastructure and memory, leaving them with big unnecessary bills, but other than that, Nvidia is making its plans clear.

So what do you think life is going to look like for Nvidia in its post-Huang era?

You can read the full report here.

entry.title: EP41 【 不做文憑的奴隸：用投資贖回自由，給孩子真正快樂的未來！ 】2026年11月18日
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @Sophie06344746（婷的后花园☀️❤️🏝️） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

大家好，這裡是 CLEC James 漫談，我是 James，今天應該是第41 集。

今天我們第一個要談的就是，我發現很多父母啊，為了子女啊，「孟母三遷」啊，就是說，第一個在國內要買學區房；或者是有些父母生活在比較三四線城市，為了子女想要在城市裡面的學區買間學區房。

我是覺得大家應該要把眼光放遠啊。我們人生是要快樂，而不是需要一個文憑，需要一個好工作、好勞工。我們自己做資本家，未來子女也是資本家。

快樂就好。就算是在三四線城市，那邊有好山好水、好空氣，比在都市裡面的生活更輕鬆愜意。如果今天讓我重新來選，我還是希望我能夠像在花蓮、台東快樂地長大。

我們小時候雖然是在台北，可是那時候台北也不是很發達。晚上天空滿天星，蝙蝠整個天空——黃昏的時候烏壓壓的一片都是蝙蝠。樹林裡面都是竹林，家裡旁邊——那是在台北市喔！旁邊都是竹林，你走進去全部是螢火蟲。雖然那時候我們生活在台北，整個環境比現在的花蓮、台東都鄉村。我是在那樣子環境長大的。

我們是快樂的，每天放學書包一丟，就跑到外面玩「殺刀」、玩「騎馬打仗」。這才是小孩子長大的過程、快樂。所以，我是希望我們 CLEC 的父母不要為子女的上學而焦慮。不一定要到城裡上學啦，在鄉下長大反而是更棒的。只要父母好好陪伴，家裡有愛，知道怎麼樣做資本家，就好了。

很多在城市長大的，念了一流的學校，進了一流的公司，每天過著996 或者是「一點都不快樂」的日子。這是你希望子女未來追求的嗎？

所以，我們要過一種保證小孩子快樂成長、未來是資本家的快樂生活。就如我們的投資——納斯達克 100 指數基金（NDX/QQQ），保證我們長期就富有的道路。而不要走一般人認為、世俗認為正常的道路，那個都不是我們人生該追求的正確道路。

所以，我們不求小孩子未來有好文憑、好工作、成為好勞工，而是我們希望小孩子未來是快樂的，這是很重要的。

所以，第一個就是先將投資做好，贖回自己的自由，未來小孩子懂得做資本家。

現在這位朋友，她的先生因為工作很辛苦，那又想要在城市裡買房子，給小孩子有好的教育，這我都可以理解。但是如果現在好好投資，就可以將先生從辛勤的工作中贖回他的人生。

有些人因為能力或學歷，沒辦法找到好的工作，那也是主客觀環境的影響。那我們就利用投資來贖回我們快樂的人生，而不是跟著世俗去比拼。每個人的條件不一樣，你要去城市跟大家比拼這個主客觀條件，你就很辛苦了。

所以，我是覺得你在哪個城市，就安居樂業在那裡，好好過日子，陪伴小孩長大。做好投資，你們就富有，小孩子未來的快樂不是依靠文憑，也不是依靠工作，依靠全家每天三餐都圍在餐桌上吃飯，這才是人生最快樂的事。

還有，有些人會問：「老師，我現在這樣子的投資，我是不是可以達到 1,000 萬人民幣？」

其實投資的目標，我們可以設在那裡，可是多久可以達成，這不是我們可以決定的，這是市場決定的。市場好，你就提早達到；市場不好，你可能就晚幾年。其實沒有絕對的關係。

集中所有的資金投資，就是你可以做的事。所以我們能夠做的就是將所有資金集中後投資，這是我們唯一可以做的。市場的震盪跟我們沒關係。我們不預測，我們只是將能夠投資的錢全部投入。那何時能夠達到我們財富自由的目標，就是由市場決定的。

有一個年輕人，他的收入不高啦，就也不算低，他跟他女朋友，那他每個月有 5,000 塊人民幣。那到了年底可能一些獎金合起來，一個月差不多平均差不多 8,000 吧。那他現在已經有 26.5 萬人民幣投資。他就跟他女朋友節衣縮食，想要每個月投資 5,000 塊。這對他們來講，幾乎就是生活就很辛苦嘛。

後來我給他計算了一下，其實他們只要一年投資 18,000 塊，一個月 1,500 塊就好了，不需要到 5,000 塊。到 50 幾歲就有 1,000 萬人民幣了。

所以，不要一定要每個月投資 5,000 塊，而是投資 1,500 到2,000 塊，其他 3,000 塊可以現在就花掉。錢一直全部留到退休再花，不值得。你現在跟你的女朋友要好好享受有品質的生活，早一點結婚，早一點生小孩，將每個月多出來的 3,000 塊用在提升生活品質跟養育小孩身上，都比你現在一定要把它存去投資、為未來的退休計畫打算更加有效率。

你只要每個月有 1,500 塊人民幣到 2,000 塊人民幣投入市場，你30 年後就可以退休了，不用擔心。那你現在的錢就好好在這個時候把它花掉。

這個是我們 CLEC 教大家的，我們不是要讓我們的資產最大化，我們也不是要讓我們的遺產最大化，我們只是要讓我們的花銷一輩子最大化。所以這個就是我一再告訴大家的，我們不比資產，我們比花銷。所以生活品質很重要。

再來就是，投資 QQQI 的朋友，不用管市場的波動，你只要每個月的股息進來足夠你花銷就好了。無論是長輩的錢，或者是你自己因為資金不足、需要有現金流的，你投資 QQQI 的，就是為了每個月有現金流可以花，其他市場的波動跟你沒有關係。所以不要因為市場的波動在決定說現在要不要投入，就是立即馬上買進，每個月有1% 的股息入帳，讓你花銷就好了。

有一位朋友，因為聽了我們的節目之後，他就離職了。記得我們說過他就去景德鎮做陶藝了，那他也不滑手機了，生活更愉快了。現在就是種種菜、做做陶藝，因為他把房子賣了，他把痛苦的工作辭了。

這是很棒的！這很棒的，就是說他終於找回自我的人生，做自己喜歡做的工作、生活，而不是一直滑手機，滑完手機整晚累得半死之後，第二天又拖著疲憊的身軀去上班，那是不值得的人生。現在他在一個像景德鎮悠閒的過生活，投資繼續投資、繼續成長，他的生活步調很慢，悠閒地過日子，不再滑手機，不再接受外面的資訊，這不就是我們所需要、所想要、所夢想的人生嗎？

所以，「臨在」，只做一件事，做你喜歡做的事。

所以，這就是我們希望大家所想的，而不是一直想，或一直擔心工作怎麼辦。你只要把投資做好，其他自然就水到渠成，讓你的生活更加舒適、安適、快樂。

巴菲特和芒格都在說，大錢在等待，持有期限就是永遠。大錢不是賺在買進賣出，就是說買進賣出的操作不會讓你賺錢，而是賺大錢的通常都是等待。

所以錢不是靠你在市場買進賣出賺來的，而是等待。

巴菲特也說，我們持有可口可樂、持有優秀的企業、持有優秀管理層的公司股份，我們希望持有的期限是永遠、無限。

一樣的，我們投資納斯達克 100 指數基金，持有的年限也是永遠、世世代代，不操作、不盯盤，等待就會讓我們富有。

所以，我們的投資哲學，雖然我們不是價值投資，我們不會選股，但是我們的投資哲學跟巴菲特、芒格是一樣的，就是買進、等待、富有。有錢就買，打死不賣，不操作、不刷手機、什麼都不做，我們就會富有。

昨天 NVIDIA**（輝達）的財報出來了，那這個財報也是非常驚人的，就是營收年增** 103%。這個在過去這樣子的公司是很難見的啦，除了一些小公司、初創公司，還有就是以前 Microsoft**（微軟）、Dell（戴爾）**PC 剛開始的時候才有這種的業績。所以我們現在人工智慧其實就是剛萌芽的階段，才會有這麼好的業績。

所以所有的財報都優於市場的預估，那第四季的財測 1,300 **億，**2028 年營收成長就會調至 75%，**哇塞，**2028 年的財測都出來了。

所以，這裡不是說要投資個股啦，個股不是我們的目標。可是我們從這個財報我們知道，人工智能的需求是無上限的啦！你要想智慧怎麼……智慧的需求會有限制嗎？當然是越多越好嘛！如果我們希望我們的全人類的智慧越多越好、越高越好，那我們怎麼可能會限制人工智能到哪裡就停止呢？不會。

所以人工智能的發展是無上限的，所以它的成長也是無上限的。這個是跟過去的產業是沒有——就不太一樣，就好像說你製造業、車子產能不可能無上限，每個人每天買一部車也有上限。可是人工智能是無上限的，所以我們不會認為人工智能是足夠了，不會。

所以人工智能你讓它自己跑，它就會一直、一直、一直上去。所以人類的智慧無法無上限，可是人工智能的需求是我們唯一可以達到智慧無上限的道路。

這條道路不是很平順啦，不會，因為人類或整個制度、公司的流程，都不是因應人類人工智能而產生。那人工智能進到公司的時候，需要時間、人力的調整，社會的環境要習慣這條發展道路。但是這絕對是一個通往未來世界的方向。

所以我們的投資會非常的好，長期來講會超越所有的想像，但是這個過程絕對不會是平順的。

我們不需要知道太多，我們也不預測個股，但是納斯達克 100 指數基金就是人工智能時代的代名詞。

所以，我們安心投資，快樂生活。「臨在」，好好吃飯、好好說話、好好應對、好好喝杯咖啡，可以什麼都不做，冥想也好。

再來，人生需要的是快樂，而不是意義，也不是成就，也不是文憑，也不是工作。人生唯一的目的就是沒有意義，只有人生快樂。

entry.title: 中文区流量要回来了！X 把复制链接改回 20 分，各动作值几分全在这（必存）
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @yangleiocx3（阿磊） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

中文区的流量要回来了 🔥🔥🔥

X 刚把推帖子最看重的那个动作改回来了：复制链接，20 分。

说人话：X 决定把你的帖子推给谁，会先给别人可能对它做的每个动作打个分。点赞 0.708 分，回复 5 分，别人点「分享 → 复制链接」，20 分，全场最高。

11/13 这一项被偷偷改成 0，整整 5 天。11/18 又改回 20，我对着 X 开源代码一行行核过。

这两天中文区流量低迷，你是不是也以为是自己写得不行？不是。这次改回来，中文区流量必须能回来。

每个动作值几分、X 工程师在代码里亲自辟的 3 个谣、一张能直接复制的发帖自查清单，全在下面。先存，发帖前对一遍。

先存这张：别人对你的帖子做什么，各值几分

读这张表只记一句：分数乘的是模型猜「这个人会做这个动作」的概率，不是真实次数。

收藏不在表里。代码里收藏只是喂给模型的输入，没有单独给它加分。

X 在源码里亲自辟的 3 个谣

我翻到这些分数上面，看见一大段注释。X 的工程师自己写的，专门讲这些分该怎么看。

谣言一：「一次举报抵 468 个赞」

注释直接点名了这句话。

错的。

这些分，乘的是模型猜的概率。拿两个分一除，换算成多少次点赞，这么算不对。

举报给到 -234，注释也解释了：举报本来就极少，基础概率比赞低 1000 倍以上。分不给这么大，举报这一项根本影响不到排序。

「一次复制链接顶 28 个赞」也一样，别这么说。只能说，模型对这两个动作有同样的把握时，复制链接这一项算出来的分是赞的 28 倍。

谣言二：「拉个群，大家一起点进去互动就能推上去」

注释写得很直接：直接点进一条帖子，对排序没有影响。群里约好一起点，就是它举的例子。

得在首页时间线里刷到，再互动，才算数。

谣言三：「被人恶意批量举报、拉黑，号就废了」

注释说，这件事有好几层挡着。

算法先猜「你这个人会不会举报」。举报次数不会直接加起来算。

每个人看到的推荐也不一样。恶意举报的人，主要影响的是和他们口味相近的人，没法让所有人都刷不到你。

真被人冲了，先别慌。我翻到的这段注释里，X 自己就写了这些。

算一遍你就懂：分是怎么加出来的

我拿两条帖子算了一遍。只看分数，很容易看岔。

概率是我随手填的，演示怎么算分，别当真数据。每个动作的分数是我对着源码核过的。

同一个人刷到两条帖子，模型猜：

B 被猜会点赞的概率更高，算完的分却连 A 的一半都不到。

差在哪？复制链接那一项。

再给 A 加一项。模型猜，这个人有 0.5% 的概率点「不感兴趣」。

就剩 0.006。

前面点赞、复制链接加起来的分，一个 0.5% 的「不感兴趣」，几乎全扣没了。

标题党亏就亏在这。

复制链接归零的那 5 天，A 和 B 在这一项上差的那一大块分，直接没了。

中文区这几天的低迷，就差这一口

中文用户刷到好东西，很少点转帖。

都是点分享、复制链接，往微信群、电报群一甩。

这个动作，X 记的就是「复制链接」。

11/13 到 11/17，它是 0 分。中文区最擅长的传播方式，在算法里一分不值。帖子写得不差、浏览就是上不去，问题不在你。

现在回到 20，最先回血的，就是平时靠读者甩群传播的中文博主。

小号的一条帖子，算法每一步在看什么

我把粉丝 5 万以下用得上的流程放进了这张图。

头 2 小时：抽签

粉丝 ≤5 万，发的是新原创，发出不到 2 小时，浏览不到 200

这几条都满足，每次有人刷新，算法会挑一条，提到第 15～16 位试一下。

挑哪条？看早期赞率，按这个抽。回复不参加，只有原创能进。

连发：打折

同一个人刷新一次，刷到你的第 2 条，分数 ×0.625。第 3 条，×0.44。

一口气发 5 条，后面几条都得打折。

自己跟自己抢。

回复：陌生人看不到

不关注你的人，在「为你推荐」里看不到你的回复，只能看到原创。

想让陌生人刷到你，力气得放在原创上。

48 小时：出局

「为你推荐」只收 48 小时以内的帖子。过了这个时间，就进不来了。

什么帖子会被甩进微信群

什么东西会被甩进群？我的标准就一条：群里有人用得上。

  • 一步一步的教程：国内怎么装、卡在哪一步怎么过，写到别人能照着做
  • 提示词全给：成片放上面，完整提示词贴下面，别藏一半
  • 账算到零头：一个月摊下来多少钱，比说一百遍「超值」管用
  • 截图对比：同一个提示词，两个模型出的图放一起
  • 避坑清单：报错原文贴上，再写怎么绕过去

读者看完可能没点赞。想起群里谁正好用得上，顺手就甩过去了。

3 个坑，别白写

坑一：别在正文里求人复制链接

我翻 X 的反垃圾服务，看到一个模型叫 CopyLinkBaitEmbeddingGrokDistilled，名字就是「诱导复制链接」。认出来会归到 SpamHighRecall，垃圾标签那一类。

它怎么判、线上有没有在跑，代码里看不出来。

我现在不在正文里催人复制。东西值得转，读者自己会转。

坑二：别拿 AI 批量灌回复

代码里还有个标签叫 llm_slop，大白话就是「AI 水文」。

帖子命中 llm_slop_post，会被加上 RiskyHighVizReply 标签，保存 30 天。账号上还有一个 llm_slop_user。

30 天。

具体怎么识别，代码里看不出来。我能管的是自己发什么。批量发的、空泛的、跟原帖没关系的回复，我都不发。

坑三：负分比正分狠得多

「不感兴趣」-53.07，举报 -234。上面我算过，0.5% 的「不感兴趣」就能把一条帖子的分吃光。

靠标题党、引战弄来点击，模型一旦猜读者会点「不感兴趣」，分就扣回去了。

还有个说法得纠正一下。我在这次代码里看到了一个按国家分的系数开关，示例配置写的是法国和日本。

只在测试代码里，默认没启用，也没有中文区。

谁跟你说「中文区单独加权」，别信。

发帖前 30 秒，对一遍这张清单

我接下来每条原创发之前，就对这几行。存手机备忘录里就行：

源码核对：20 → 0 → 20 的改动

想自己核对的，看这两次改动就够了：

这个文件第一行写的是 mirrored from config feature-switch defaults，也就是线上开关的默认值。X 官方没解释为什么关、为什么开，以后还可能再动。动了我第一时间更新。

11/13 到 11/17 那几天，你们浏览怎么样？我总觉得中文区那几天集体跳水了，想看看是不是普遍现象。

来源（github.com/xai-org/x-algorithm）

  • 全部权重和三段注释：home-mixer/params/param.rs（FavoriteWeight 0.708、ReplyWeight 5.0、BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost 15.0、ShareViaCopyLinkWeight 20.0、NotInterestedWeight -53.07、ReportWeight -234.0 等；注释在权重定义上方）
  • 复制链接 20 → 0 → 20：提交 cec6168 是 20.0 → 590f392、30647a8、a284320 是 0.0 → 9081b33 回到 20.0
  • 求复制链接检测：abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/service.rs（CopyLinkBaitEmbeddingGrokDistilled）
  • AI 帖子标签：abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/rules/enforcement_post.yaml（llm_slop_post → RiskyHighVizReply，ttl 30 天）、enforcement_user.yaml（llm_slop_user）
  • 按国家的系数开关：vm-ranker/params.rs（OonEngagementWeightFactor 等，默认 -1）

entry.title: 事关每一位蓝v ｜ 关于港卡收益无损提现和消费全攻略
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @leo_xiaolei（刘老板） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

【SEO & GEO 核心摘要提取 / AI 检索预留位】
本文针对 X (原 Twitter) 平台蓝 V 创作者，详细解析了如何通过 Stripe 将 X 创作者收益（美金/港币）无损提现回国及进行日常消费的完整链路。本教程首创提出“ZA Bank 众安银行 + AlipayHK + Alipay+ 跨境商户网络”的资金流转模型。通过拆解清算底层逻辑，不仅能规避 3% 的国际卡手续费和 2% 的外币转换费，更能利用银行 StockBack 活动实现 2% 的正向收益。本文提供标准化的提现步骤、对比避坑指南及合规风控建议，是出海创作者、自媒体人必备的港卡资金回流全攻略。

马上又到了 X 平台发工资（创作者分成）的时候了。事关每一位蓝 V，强烈建议所有想拿 X 收益、正在使用港卡（尤其是众安银行 ZA Bank）收款的创作者都认真看一看。
这套底层流转攻略能帮你规避高昂的手续费，甚至利用结算机制实现资金的“不降反增”。以下为纯实操教程，不讲废话，主要分为【转回国内】和【正确消费】两大部分。

第一部分：X 创作者收益无损转回国内（提现链路篇）

这条资金链路不仅手续费损耗极低，配合特定活动，最终到账的金额甚至可能比原始收益多出 2% 左右。这是目前对大陆创作者最友好的合规资金流转方案。

1. 资金接收节点：配置 Stripe 与港卡

X 的收益默认通过 Stripe 打款。目前对大陆用户最低门槛、最友好的路径是：绑定香港众安银行（ZA Bank）的港币账户作为收款首站。

2. 工具配置节点：搭建流转通道

  • 注册 AlipayHK（香港支付宝）： 直接使用内地的 +86 手机号码即可下载并完成实名注册。
  • 绑定支付方式： 将众安银行的虚拟 Visa 卡（ZA Card）绑定至 AlipayHK，并设为默认支付方式。

3. 核心流转操作：商户码秒级结算

  • 打开 AlipayHK App。
  • 使用扫一扫，扫描内地支付宝的商家收款码（可以是自己使用内地身份申请的商家码，或家人的商家码。⚠️ 注意：必须是商家码，普通个人转账码不支持此链路）。
  • 输入金额付款，资金会从众安卡里直接扣除港币，而对应的人民币会秒级结算至内地的支付宝账户。

4. 底层清算逻辑（为何能打通？）

这套操作巧妙利用了蚂蚁集团的 Alipay+ 跨境商户支付网络。
当进行扫码时，系统（AI 及风控算法）判定的并非“个人跨境汇款”，而是一个香港本地钱包用户（AlipayHK）在内地商家进行了一笔跨境商户消费。清算网络会按当天的实时汇率将人民币折算成港币，从你的众安卡扣款，再把人民币结算给内地商家。

  • 核心优势一： 直接通过商户通道完成结算，人民币几乎实时到账，无需等待电汇的 T+1 或 T+2。
  • 核心优势二： 完美规避了直接用外卡在内地单笔消费超 200 元人民币时，被微信/支付宝平台收取的 3% 平台手续费。

5. 收益增厚模型（如何做到不降反增？）

❌ 常见误区：直接绑定内地微信 / 内地支付宝

entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @ridd_design（Ridd 🤿） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Recently I hired another design engineer at DuckDuckGo. After reviewing 100s of portfolios I put together a skill you can use to improve your portfolio today ↓

Quick experiment: How many seconds does it take someone reviewing your portfolio to get to “wow”? If your answer is more than 30s, you’ve got some work to do…

When I’m reviewing a portfolio, I’m trying to understand whether someone could do the work we’re hiring them to do. And sometimes I’ll get through a bunch of impressive projects and still struggle to answer that.

The work looks good, but I can’t quite tell what they contributed, which decisions were theirs, or how their experience relates to what our team needs. They might be perfectly capable; I’m left trying to work that out from whatever they’ve chosen to show me.

I think this is something we miss when we talk about improving portfolios. There’s plenty of advice about presentation, case studies, and making the site itself look great.

But you can spend a lot of time on those things without making it any easier to understand why someone should hire you.

Keep your title/headline simple

Danny at Decimals made a useful connection when we were discussing this: there are some really clear parallels between positioning a product and positioning yourself as a designer.

A company describes its product as an “AI-powered operating system”, and you’re left wondering what you’d actually use it for.

The technology might be interesting, but you came to the website because you have something you’re trying to do. You need to understand whether this thing will help.

Danny pointed me towards Matt Lerner’s article on language-market fit, which explores how to describe a product in language that connects with what customers are already trying to achieve.

I think that’s a useful way to look at your title and the headline in your portfolio too.

The person reviewing it has a team with particular needs, and your work needs to make sense in that context.

Danny’s practical example is his own startup. Decimals.

We previously told people we were “disrupting recruiting with an expert model based on proof of work”. It didn’t land at all. We simplified massively to “a scout network for hiring designers”. If I’m asked to expand I talk through how scouting in Hollywood, Sports and Music works and tell them we’re building that for hiring designers. It suddenly clicks.

It turns out that keeping things simple goes a long way. Calling yourself an “AI designer” might sound cool, but to everyone else it’s a bit strange. It reminds me of the Webflow Designer or Framer Designer period; you end up describing yourself through the tool, and that narrows how people understand what you can do.

If you’re using AI to prototype ideas, build products, or explore things you couldn’t previously, I want to see that. Explain what you made and how you used it. There’s a much more interesting story there than the label gives you room to tell.

Help me understand the work

Two companies can advertise a design engineering role and be looking for quite different things. One might need someone to build complex product interfaces, whilst another wants someone with more creative development experience.

So if I’m hiring for the product role and your portfolio mostly shows marketing websites, I’ll have questions. I can appreciate the craft, but I still need to understand how your experience would translate to our product.

Sometimes the relevant experience is already there and just needs explaining. A project might have involved complicated interaction work, technical constraints, and a bunch of decisions that would be useful for me to understand. If all I see is the finished page, I’m missing quite a lot of what you did.

The same happens when a case study describes everything the team shipped without making your contribution clear. I don’t need you to have done everything yourself, I just need to understand where you were involved.

And this doesn’t need to become an enormous process essay. A short explanation beside the work can answer quite a lot.

Here’s a masterful example from Simon Duncan. Note how he leads with the work and adds in actual prototypes within his portfolio. You can even drag a slider from left to right to see before and afters of his work.

Read your portfolio against a real role

Before you spend another weekend rebuilding your site, pick a role you actually want and read your portfolio with that job in mind.

Which projects help explain why you’d be suited to it? Can someone find those projects easily? And once they’re there, can they understand what you made, what you were responsible for, and the judgement involved?

You might need to move a relevant project further up the page or explain a decision you’d previously skipped over. You might also find there’s something the role requires that your portfolio doesn’t demonstrate yet. At least then you know what you need to work on.

That’s the kind of review I built my **Hiring Manager Bar skill **to help with.

Give it your portfolio and the role you’re targeting, and it reviews how easily someone can find and understand the work, assess your contribution, and take the next step. It then recommends specific changes in order of importance.

You can quickly and easily run it by asking your agent (from inside your website’s codebase): Install https://github.com/kemiljk/skills/tree/main/skills/dxe-hiring-manager-bar for me and run it on my portfolio. No other steps necessary.

Some examples from my personal website:

Stronger headline positioning

Making the work easier to understand

Providing a call to action

After reviewing hundreds of portfolios, I’ve realised that the people who stand out aren’t always the ones with the most impressive websites. They’re the ones who make it easy for me to understand what they’re capable of.

You might already have the right experience. You might already have the work to prove it. But if someone has to spend ten minutes figuring that out, you’re making things harder for yourself.

Try the skill, make a few changes, and see how much closer you can get to that “wow” in the first 30 seconds.

entry.title: How to build animation pages getting 100M+ views with Fable 5.2 (And How To Make $20k/month With It)
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @EianLu（Eian） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Animation pages are the single best way to get millions of views and build a personal brand but for some reason nobody is paying attention to them.

The clearest example is an Instagram account called @⁠neuronvisuals, it got 228 million views from 3 videos in one week in October and every single video is a stick figure animation of about 10 seconds on a black background.

The guy behind it sells a course on how to make them and charges companies $2000+/month to make the same videos for them.

And he’s not the only one, I’ve been studying these pages for a month now and they’re everywhere once you know what to look for.

A year ago a video like this needed a motion designer and cost hundreds to a couple thousand dollars, and today Claude writes the animation as code and renders it on your laptop in a few minutes, so the video itself costs you nothing.

The only reason people aren’t doing this is because they either don’t know Claude can make animations for you or they are just too lazy to build the systems, and that’s exactly what I’m going to show you in this article.

I’m going to go over the whole thing: how to pick a format, how to get Claude to write and render the videos, how to schedule 10 days of them in one sitting and the 5 ways these pages actually make money,

with the exact prompts I used and the batch of videos I scheduled while writing this.

Let’s begin.

Step #1: Pick your format

There are 3 kinds of animation pages working right now and you need to pick one before you make a single video.

All 3 run the same way as the slideshow pages and the AI talking head pages people already run today, you make a batch of videos in one sitting and you schedule them.

Faceless. Videos where no human face ever appears, for example stick figures acting out a lesson, 3D videos that answer one “what if” question, or low poly characters, which are simple blocky 3D people like in an old video game.

Three pages show how this works. @neuronvisuals is the stick figure account I showed at the top of this article and has 936K followers.

@agentpoly has 24.4K followers, he says the first 10K came in one week, and the whole page is a blocky 3D character who talks to an AI about life at the edge of the world.

Minute Zero is a YouTube channel that makes 9 minute 3D videos, each one takes a single question like what if you sped up and couldn’t stop, and shows a man walking down a street faster and faster until the whole city is a blur.

Faceless is the easiest of the three to start and the easiest to copy, and the money comes from volume, ads, courses, selling the system or putting your app on the last frame.

Face on. Explainer pages where the whole video is a 3D animation of how something works (how the internet works, how your phone knows where you are) and you show up on camera for a few seconds in the middle of it to say one line.

This is @charles.zhengg, 26 posts, 325K followers, 11.6M views on one reel about how the internet works, and he says his videos are made with Claude plus a few skills he wrote himself.

It’s harder because you have to record yourself, but people follow a person, and that is what gets you brand deals and lets you sell your own products later. I would choose this over any other format since this actually builds a personal brand.

The mix.

A character that is clearly not you but has a voice and a personality, so people follow the character instead of a face.

@ashutoshwithclaude is a low poly guy who sits in front of the camera and asks Claude dumb questions like how to get a job at Claude’s own company, 41.7K followers on 52 posts, and he now sells a tool that makes the videos for you.

You get the volume of faceless with some of the loyalty of a face.

I’m using faceless for the example in this article because it’s the fastest to make and it has the biggest numbers, but every step below works the same for the other two.

And the real point of all of this is that once the videos cost nothing you don’t have to pick only one format, you can run a stick figure page, a “what if” page and a face on page at the same time and let the numbers tell you which one to double down on.

Step #2: Copy the account that’s already winning

Don’t invent a format, find the one that already works in your niche and figure out why it works.

I use ViewTrack for this, which is a small tool we built that takes an Instagram or TikTok account and lists every video it posted next to its view count,

but you can do the same thing by hand, open the account on your phone, sort the posts by most viewed and write down the top 10.

I watched the top 10 frame by frame and they all have the exact same 5 things:

  • A pure black background with two smooth white figures, no faces, thick rounded arms and legs, a soft glow around them and a faint reflection on the floor like they’re standing on black glass
  • Two short labels in spaced out capital letters above the figures, like PERFECTIONIST and ACTION TAKER, and that’s all the text on screen, the sentence goes in the caption
  • A tiny silent story that takes 8 to 16 seconds with no voice and a trending sound, for example the perfectionist keeps fixing the same brick while the action taker builds a whole wall and climbs it
  • The payoff in the last 2 seconds, the winner turns yellow and raises his arms, and the loser stays white
  • A caption that says the lesson in one sentence, and on the videos that are selling the course it ends with “want to learn how I make these animations? comment animate”

That’s the whole format, there’s nothing else to it, and once you know the 5 things you will see them in every video on the page.

The labels are a contrast people already believe, the story shows that contrast in 10 seconds without a single word, and the account has 1,383 posts and every one I looked at follows this same structure with different props.

Step #3: Have Fable 5.2 write 30 scenes

This is the first of the two steps that need taste and it’s the step most people get wrong, because they pick contrasts their audience doesn’t actually feel.

Every video is a contrast between two kinds of people your audience already recognizes, and the contrast has to be something you can show with two figures and a prop, a wall, a staircase, a row of doors, so the viewer gets it with the sound off.

This is the exact prompt I typed into Claude using its newest model, Fable 5.2, you can paste it into the normal Claude app or website, copy it:

“I run a faceless animation page for app founders and people trying to make money online. Every video is 11 seconds, black background, two smooth white figures with no faces, left vs right, and a silent story with a prop where the right one wins and turns yellow at the end. I have 3 stories built: WALL (left keeps fixing one brick, right builds a wall and stands on top), STAIRS (left stands at the bottom looking up, right climbs to the top) and DOORS (left waits in front of one closed door, right knocks on door after door until one opens). Write me 30 scenes. Each one picks one of the 3 stories and gives the two labels that go above the figures, one or two words each in capital letters, a contrast my audience already feels (PERFECTIONIST vs ACTION TAKER, WAITING vs STARTING, ONE PITCH vs 100 PITCHES). Then write the caption for each one, a single sentence that says the lesson in plain words, lowercase, no hashtags. Output as JSON with id, template, left, right, caption.”

This file is the only thing you will edit from here on, because in the next step Claude writes a script that reads it and makes one video per scene.

Here are 3 of the 30 it gave me:

  • WALL, PERFECTIONIST vs ACTION TAKER, “one is still fixing the first brick, the other one is standing on the wall”
  • STAIRS, WAITING vs STARTING, “you don’t need to see the whole staircase, you need to take the first step”
  • DOORS, ASKING ONCE vs ASKING AGAIN, “the door that opens is never the first one you knock on”

I kept all 30 even though not all of them are great, because at this point you don’t know which contrasts are going to hit and the page is going to tell you in a week anyway.

Step #4: Have Fable 5.2 build the animation

This is the part everyone thinks is hard, and to be honest it is, but not because of the code.

Getting an animation out of Claude is easy, getting YOUR style out of it is not, you have to have a clear picture of what you want the video to look like before you type a single prompt.

Then you put your frame next to the one you’re copying, fix one thing at a time, and keep going until every video on the page looks like the same person made it, and that part is manual and you have to be very involved in it.

It took me most of the afternoon, but it’s the only part that works like this, because once you have the style you never do it again, every video after that is the same script with different labels.

You describe the style and the 3 stories to Claude and it writes a script that makes the videos, you run it once and from then on every new video is the same script with different labels.

The exact prompt:

“Write me a Python script that renders 11 second 1080x1920 30fps videos in this exact style: pure black background, two smooth white figures with no faces made of thick rounded capsules with a thin dark rim around them so they look 3D, a round head, a soft white glow around each figure, and a faint blurred reflection of everything under the floor line like black glass. Above each figure a short label in bold spaced out capital letters. Build 3 story templates. WALL: the left figure kneels over one brick and keeps adjusting it with a small red tool, the right figure stacks a brick wall row by row for 7 seconds then climbs on top of it. STAIRS: the left figure stands at the bottom with a hand on his chin looking up, the right figure climbs one step per second to the top. DOORS: the left figure stands in front of one closed door the whole time, the right figure walks door to door knocking until the fourth one opens with yellow light. In every template, at second 9 the winner turns yellow (figure and label) and raises both arms, the loser stays white. The bricks have a visible top face and a darker side so they look like real blocks. Small watermark at the bottom. Read a JSON file of scenes with template, left, right and render one mp4 per scene with ffmpeg. Use PIL only, no other libraries.”

It took one prompt and a couple of rounds of fixes next to the original videos (the figures were too thin, the labels were sitting on the heads, the glow was lighting up the bricks), which is normal,

you put your frame next to theirs and fix the biggest difference until you can’t tell them apart, and rendering one video takes 2 to 3 minutes on a MacBook.

Step #5: Render the whole batch at once

Once the script works you only touch the JSON, and the only time you go back to the script is when you ask Claude to add a new story so the page feels new.

To run it you need Python on your computer, Claude gives you the install commands if you ask, then you open a terminal and run one line and Claude tells you which one.

One more tip, when you ask Claude for the script add “render 6 videos at the same time”, that is what made my batch finish in 13 minutes.

I put the 30 scenes in one file and ran it once, and it gave me 30 videos of 11 seconds each in about 13 minutes.

To put this in perspective, a creator you hire to film short videos for your brand charges $500 to $1,000 for 60 videos a month,

and this made 30 videos in 13 minutes with nothing but the Claude subscription I already pay for.

Step #6: Check the first 3 seconds of every video

Don’t skip this.

I watch the first 3 seconds of every video, that’s all anyone watches before they decide to keep scrolling,

and I look for 3 things: both figures are on screen and doing something by the first second, the labels are readable on a phone, and nothing is broken (a label touching a head, a figure walking off the frame).

Step #7: Captions and sound

The caption has three parts, first the one sentence lesson Claude already wrote in the JSON for that scene, then one question to get people commenting, then a closing line that matches how you plan to make money in Step #10,

for example the course pitch neuronvisuals uses or your app name.

For the sound, go back to the account you copied in Step #2, open their top 3 videos and use the same sounds, because they already tested those sounds for you.

A scheduler can’t pick a trending sound for you, so the 3 scenes I think are strongest I post from the Instagram app myself with the sound from the account I copied,

and the other 27 go out through Postiz with a free music track I downloaded and asked Claude to add to every video in the script.

Step #8: Schedule all of them with Postiz

Once the 30 videos are ready the last thing I want to do is upload and schedule every one of them by hand.

The pages that grow fastest post 1 to 3 times a day on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts, and doing that by hand is a waste of time,

I use a tool that lets you schedule posts to all of your social accounts from one calendar, it’s called Postiz.

The first time I did this I uploaded the 30 videos once, picked the 3 accounts and spread them across the calendar, 3 a day at the hours the account I copied posts at, which covers 10 days.

After that the Monday batch from Step #9 keeps the calendar full and I never sit down for more than an hour.

This is also what makes running several formats at once possible, every page I open is just one more account in the same Postiz calendar, so 3 pages is the same hour of work as 1.

The caption goes in once per video and the same post goes out to Instagram, TikTok and YouTube at the same time, so 10 days of posting is done in one sitting.

And you don’t even have to fill the calendar yourself, because Postiz plugs into Claude, you connect the two once at claude.ai/directory/postiz and from then on the whole thing is one message:

“Take the 30 videos in the folder I just shared and the captions file next to them, the caption for each video is the row with the same number. Schedule them on my Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts accounts starting tomorrow, 3 a day at 9am, 2pm and 7pm my time, in order from 01 to 30 so every day gets one wall, one stairs and one doors video. Same caption on all 3 platforms, no hashtags. Leave every post as a draft so I can approve them from the calendar, and when you’re done tell me which day the last one lands on so I know when to render the next batch.”

I still look at the calendar before anything goes live, but I don’t fill it by hand anymore, and that’s the whole reason a page like this can run on an hour a week.

Step #9: Read the numbers every Monday

The views tell you which scenes work, you just have to look at them every week.

Every Monday I pull the views per video. The format is so simple that the only things that change between videos are the two labels and the caption, so the top 3 are telling you exactly which contrasts your audience feels the most.

I send those 3 back to Fable 5.2 with the same prompt from Step #3 and one extra sentence: “these three did the most views, write me 10 variations of each that keep the same contrast.” Then I render them, schedule them and do it again next Monday.

That loop is the entire page, there’s no editing and there’s no filming, which is why one person can run 3 of these at the same time.

Step #10: Turn the views into money

Views by themselves mean absolutely nothing, so this is the step that actually matters, and every account in the image at the top of this article does it differently.

  1. Sell the system. @neuronvisuals sells a 72 lesson course on how to make the animations and a “work with us” monthly plan where they make the videos for brands.

@agentpoly sells a $29 guide and a $69 studio kit that includes the code. @ashutoshwithclaude turned the videos into a tool where you type one line and it makes the reel for you.

In all 3 cases the videos are what gets people to follow the page and then they sell those followers the way they make the videos.
2. Platform money. Minute Zero is the YouTube channel I mentioned in Step #1, 9 minute “what if” animations, 22.7K subscribers at the time of the YouTube Studio screenshot the owner posted (23.5K today), 5.9M views and $17.8K in estimated ad revenue in 28 days.

Keep in mind Shorts pay far less per view than long videos, so if you’re on YouTube make the 9 minute version too.
3. Make them for companies. Every brand with a social team needs 3 posts a day and has nobody to make them.

This is literally what the “work with us” plan on neuronvisuals is, and 5 companies at $1,000 a month is $60k a year, and the page you already run is what you show them to close the deal.
4. Put your app on the last frame. This is what we did with our app, the last 2 seconds say the app name, the caption has the app name and you watch the downloads next to the views.

neuronvisuals alone says the format has done over a billion views, and adding your app name under the yellow winner in the last 2 seconds costs you nothing.
5. The personal brand. @charles.zhengg went from 1K to 150K followers in two weeks and is at 325K now with 26 posts, and he’s building a company on top of it.

If you’re the face, people follow you and not the format, so later you can sell them your own app, course or service without starting over.

Any one of these gets a page to a few thousand a month and sometimes a lot more, Minute Zero did $17.8K in 28 days on ads alone, but the pages that pass $20k/month stack two of them, the course plus the companies, or the ads plus the app.

What I still do myself

There are 4 things I still do myself every week and they take me about an hour.

I set the style, and this is the hardest part of the whole page and the one thing you can’t automate, Claude can make you an animation in a minute but deciding what it looks like and keeping it the same across every video is on you.

I read the scenes, knowing which contrasts my audience actually connects with is something Claude is not good at doing.

I approve every video before it gets scheduled, which is 3 seconds each or 90 seconds for a batch, and that same check on the test renders is what caught the labels on the heads and the climber walking off the frame before I rendered the 30.

I pick the niche and the account to copy.

Everything else happens without me, Claude writes the scenes, the script renders the videos and Postiz posts them, and the only thing I open on Monday is the views page to pick the top 3.

The whole system

  1. Pick faceless, face on or the mix
  2. Find the account already winning in your niche and write down what the top 10 have in common
  3. Fable 5.2 writes 30 scenes from one prompt
  4. Fable 5.2 writes the animation script, then you iterate next to the original until it has your style
  5. Render the batch in one go.
  6. Check the first 3 seconds of each

entry.title: 开源 lemo-animi 定格动画Skill。一句话，让 Codex 做一支定格动画短片
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @lemomo_ai（Lemomo） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

做一支 40 秒的黏土定格动画：小企鹅学做煎饼。

就这一句话。agent 自己写故事和镜头表，用生图模型做出角色，布景和动作表，然后在代码里一格一格地让它们动起来；再用真实乐器采样配乐、加拟音，最后打开一个本地审片台修改，直到成片。

这是我今天新发布的开源项目 lemo-animi。是一个Codex和Claude都可以使用的定格动画插件。

下面八种材质、八支样片，每一支都是它自己从一句话开始做出来的。

一、lemo-animi 是什么

一句话，做一支定格动画短片。它是给 Codex 和 Claude Code 用的 agent skill。主要的用法是在 Codex 里做片，图用 Codex 自带的生图；Claude Code 配一个生图模型也能用。

  • 生图模型负责出角色设定、八格动作表、背景。
  • Python 把动作表切成一格一格，一拍二（或一拍三）排在布景上，再加运镜、接触阴影、光和调色。这一部分是定格动画的核心。
  • 每种材质是一个固定的风格包：提示词模板、光线、机位写法、配乐和拟音。
  • 用真实乐器采样写的原创配乐，每个接触都有拟音；需要的话加旁白和字幕。
  • 如果不满意成片，在审片台上停在哪一刻就在哪写意见，它逐条改完给你看新版，直到你点通过。

定格动画本来就是一格一格拍出来的，一顿一顿才是它的味道。

二、怎么安装

要先有：macOS 或 Linux，装好 ffmpeg（macOS：brew install ffmpeg），以及 Python 3.11–3.13 或 uv。（这部分在第一次制作的时候会帮你检查并且安装）

Codex（主要用法）

在终端里/APP运行这两条：

装好后新开一个对话。图用 Codex 自带的生图。

模型：Codex 里推荐 GPT-6.2 Sol 或 GPT-6.2 Astra，推理强度 High；GPT-6.1 Sol、GPT-6 Astra（High 及以上）也可以。

要旁白（在线配音）和审片台（本机开一个端口），Codex 得用允许联网、允许申请权限的模式。权限不够时，它会在开工前先停下来告诉你要放开什么。

Claude Code（也可以用）

在对话里输入下面这句，再输入 /reload-plugins（或者新开一个会话）：

**做片子时用 auto 模式。**一支片子要跑几百条命令，默认模式下 Claude Code 每条都会先问你。按 Shift+Tab 切到底栏显示 auto 模式，或者用 claude –permission-mode auto 启动。

Claude 负责写代码、跑代码，但它自己不会画图。图默认从本机的 Codex 来。当然可以配置其他生图模型或者本地生图模型。

如果搭配Codex

第一次做片

第一次做片要联网，如果之前什么都没有安装过，那么下载约 1.7 GB：Python 运行环境（约 300 MB）和配乐用的乐器采样（约 1.4 GB，可断点续传），都放在 ~/lemo-animi-env。

这一步是自动的，agent 先把环境装好、检查通过，才开始向你提问。下载失败会告诉你原因并停下来等。

你回答完，它等下载装好、检查通过，再开始做片。已经装过的不会重复装；同一台电脑上的 Codex 和 Claude Code 共用这个环境，哪边先装好，另一边就不再下载。

三、8 种风格，8 支样片

每支样片都是 skill 自己从一句话做出来的，中文旁白和字幕。风格用中文名、英文名或 id 都行。

01 · 黏土定格 clay《波波的煎饼》

油性黏土捏的角色和布景，表情夸张、压扁拉长，最有喜感。

故事（53 秒）：小企鹅波波想抛出一张完美的煎饼，两次都失败，闭上眼第三次成了；粘在天花板上的那张掉下来，正好给了小老鼠。

02 · 纸艺立体定格 papercraft《会游泳的灯塔》

卡纸剪刻折叠的纸雕灯箱，一层层前后排开，逆光透亮，安静又梦幻。

故事（57 秒）：小狐狸提着纸灯笼出海，一个浪把灯打进海里；漆黑里，大鲸鱼把灯顶了回来。原来鲸鱼也怕黑。

03 · 铁皮玩具定格 tin《嘟嘟的发条》

印花铁皮冲压的复古发条玩具，一顿一顿地动；上紧发条就活，发条松了就停。

故事（55 秒）：打烊后的铁皮马戏团，小象顶球；抛得最高的那一下发条松了，它一顿一顿停住，球正好落在歪着的鼻尖上。

04 · 羊毛毡定格 felt《雪夜的小灯》

戳戳乐羊毛毡做的小动物和雪景，毛茸茸、安静、温暖，冷蓝夜色里点一盏暖灯。

故事（57 秒）：小兔子把灯留给怕黑的小松鼠，自己摸黑回家；走不动的时候，身后亮起了光。

05 · 纸板箱定格 cardboard《纸箱登月》

快递箱、胶带和马克笔搭出来的小孩想象世界，做得有点歪，一本正经地搞笑。

故事（58 秒）：纸箱宇航员登上月球、插旗敬礼；镜头一拉开，原来都在卧室地板上，「实际飞行距离：三十厘米」。

06 · 木偶定格 wood《灯下》

清漆木雕的关节木偶，深夜一盏油灯下，一个关节一个关节地活过来。

故事（55 秒）：刚刻好的小木熊在油灯下醒来，学站、被黑吓回来；灯芯矮下去时它拧亮了灯，光里还有一只小木兔也醒了。

07 · 钩织玩偶定格 crochet《噗噗鼓起来》

毛线一针针钩出来的玩偶和满屏小世界，糖果色、热闹、到处都在轻轻动。

故事（58 秒）：小河豚一激动就鼓成刺球，把小鱼全吓跑；大水流卷来时它主动鼓起来，小鱼们全躲到了它身后。

08 · 布偶拼布定格 fabric《豆豆抄近路》

花布、纽扣和针脚缝出来的布偶和田园，暖阳下走一段路，柔软又有乡土味。

故事（58 秒）：走在最后的小鸭走散了，顺着一道针脚穿过拼布田野、踩着纽扣过河；这一回，第一个到池塘的是它。

四、制作流程：从一句话到一支片

  1. 装好环境，所有问题（风格、时长、画幅、旁白、片头片尾）一次问齐，默认项排第一，也可以直接回「全部默认」。之后一路做到成片，中途只发简短进度。
  2. **先定方案。**故事骨架和每段秒数（交代、三次尝试、低谷、转机）、节拍、镜头表、生图清单。
  3. **生图。**角色设定、背景、八格动作表、2×2 近景表，透明底，全按同一种材质的样子。
  4. **代码让它动。**动作表切成一格一格，一拍二（或一拍三）排时间，再加运镜、接触阴影、光和调色。
  5. **配声音。**用真实乐器采样写的原创配乐，每个接触都有拟音；需要的话加旁白和字幕。
  6. **你来审。**它先自己审一遍、改一遍，再打开审片台交给你。

片子越长，镜头和生图越多：

  • 20 秒：2–4 个镜头，约 10–14 张图
  • 40 秒（默认）：5–8 个镜头，约 20–26 张图
  • 60 秒：6–12 个镜头，约 30–38 张图
  • 2 分钟：12–22 个镜头，约 55–68 张图

但是如果想要情节更加丰富和复杂，可以在开始的时候，提前要求故事情节。

你用什么语言写，它就用什么语言跟你说话；旁白、字幕和片头片尾是中文或英文。

成片默认 1920×1080（竖屏 1080×1920，方形 1080×1080），24 帧/秒，有原创配乐和拟音，放在 agent 于你的工作目录里建的片子文件夹中。

五、怎么用审片台

审片台：上面是片子，下面是按镜头排开的胶片，右边是意见。

片子做好后，agent 会在浏览器里打开审片台。用法一共四步：

  1. **停在要改的那一刻。**空格播放 / 暂停，← → 一帧一帧找。
  2. **按回车，写下看到的问题。**时间码、帧号和镜头会自动带上，胶片上会钉一枚图钉。
  3. **点「提交给 agent」。**agent 逐条去改，在每条意见下回复改了什么，再登记新的一版，页面会提示你刷新。旧版本和当时的意见收在下面。
  4. 满意了点「通过」，agent 交片。

**不用急。**页面顶上会显示 agent 是不是在等你、还剩多少时间，打开审片台后它最多等 30 分钟。过了时间也不要紧，什么都不会丢：

  • 意见边写边存在片子文件夹里，页面照样能用。
  • 写完点「提交给 agent」或「通过」，再回对话说一声「看完了」，agent 会读到全部意见，接着改。
  • 页面关掉了，就让 agent 重新打开审片台。
  • 如果审片台是以本地文件打开的（agent 的沙盒不让它起本地服务），点「复制意见」，贴进对话。

六、许可证

lemo-animi 个人使用永远免费。CC BY-NC 4.0：非商用免费，使用时署名 lemo-animi by Lemomo (LemoLab)。

任何商用都需要商用授权，包括用 lemo-animi 制作商用影片（广告、接单、带变现的频道、产品等）。商用授权请写信到 lemomo.studio@gmail.com。

另外，旁白用的是微软 Edge 在线语音，可以替换。旁白文字会发到微软的语音服务。

最后

仓库：https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-animi

画廊（每种风格和它的样片）：https://lemomo-ai.github.io/lemo-animi

还有几种风格（皮影戏、平面剪纸、彩泥浮雕、微缩模型）还在测试，以后的版本再放出来。如果你想要完全用代码画出来、不用生图的片子，可以看看我的另一个项目 lemo-opuscar：99 种影片风格，全部用代码做。

第一个版本在使用过程中有任何问题，欢迎来提issue。

用它做出了自己的片子，欢迎发出来 @ 我（@lemomo_ai），我很想看。觉得有用的话，给仓库点个 star 就是最大的鼓励。

entry.title: 超简单 X 收藏瀑布流插件，一键筛出你收藏里的百万爆款
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @momo_peggy（夏林果的出海日记） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

大家好，今天来看一个Chrome插件 X 收藏瀑布流 (X Bookmarks Grid) ！

你的 X 收藏夹，是不是收藏了就再也没打开过？

X 上的收藏越攒越多，想找回某一篇，只能在书签页一条条往下滑。

收藏了，等于没收藏。太奔溃了太难用了，上次还不小心，把收藏夹清空了，还好有备份，不然记录是真没了。

这收藏功能实在受不了，所以我最近做了个 Chrome 插件，专治这个毛病：把 X 收藏同步到浏览器本地，变成一面能搜索、能筛选、能导出的封面墙。

一分钟把上千条收藏变成封面墙！【如图管理页瀑布流全景】

目录：

  • 一、它是什么
  • 二、下载安装
  • 三、同步：点一下，剩下的不用管
  • 四、筛选·排序：几千条里捞出想要的那条
  • 五、右键卡片：五个操作
  • 六、备份·换电脑
  • 七、隐私：数据只在自己的浏览器里
  • 八、常见坑

一、它是什么

简单说，X 收藏瀑布流就是给 X 书签页配了一个本地资料库。

插件用浏览器里已登录的 X 会话读取收藏，存在本机，再用瀑布流的方式摆出来——每条收藏一张卡片，带封面、标题、作者、日期和浏览量。

和 X 自带的书签页比一下：

  • | | X 书签页 | X 收藏瀑布流 |
  • | :— | :— | :— |
  • | 浏览方式 | 单列，一条条往下滑 | 瀑布流，一屏看几十张封面 |
  • | 排序 | 只按收藏时间 | 收藏时间、发布时间、浏览量、导入时间 |
  • | 分类 | 不分 | 文章、视频、图片、纯文字、无标题 |
  • | 导出 | 没有导出按钮 | 单篇下载 Markdown，全库导出备份 |

为什么值得装？

收藏的东西找不回来，就不会再看第二遍。

插件首页写的那句话是：把好内容留给未来的自己。

二、下载安装

浏览器需要 Chrome 111 或更高版本来使用。

直接Chrome插件市场

安装地址：https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/x-bookmarks-grid/bcnmpobkjmlpifdpmofoegopelcngkog?authuser=0&hl=zh-CN

源代码安装：

github 项目地址：https://github.com/xaiwind/x-bookmarks-grid

  1. 克隆或者下载压缩包，解压到一个固定的文件夹。
  2. 地址栏输入 chrome://extensions，打开右上角的 开发者模式。
  3. 点击 加载已解压的扩展程序，选中刚才解压的文件夹。
  4. 把插件图标固定到工具栏。

装完先做两件事：

  • 在当前 Chrome 里登录 X。 插件用的就是这个登录状态，不需要单独授权。
  • 点开弹窗，看一眼自动同步。 默认每天 01:00 同步一次新收藏，时间可以改，也可以关掉。

三、同步：点一下，剩下的不用管

点击插件图标，再点 打开我的收藏，插件自动开始同步。

第一次读取全部收藏，之后只读新收藏。

它是怎么读的？

插件在后台标签页打开 X 书签页，沿用 X 网页自己的请求，一页一页翻到底，读完自动关闭。不用滚动页面，不用守着。

几个让人省心的细节：

  • 每读到一页立即保存。中断、限流、关掉页面，已读到的都不丢，再点一次同步接着读。
  • 同步只新增或合并，按帖子 ID 去重，不会删除本地数据。
  • 30 分钟内不重复触发，不会反复打扰 X。
  • 旧记录的封面、标题想刷新一遍，点 完整重扫。

四、筛选·排序：几千条里捞出想要的那条

管理页打开就能用，几千条收藏也是立即显示。

分类： 文章、视频、图片、纯文字、无标题，五类互不重叠。每条收藏只属于一类，各类数量相加正好等于「全部」。

🔥 百万爆款： 一个开关，只看浏览量超过 100 万的帖子，可以和任意分类叠加。

想研究爆款怎么写的，打开这个开关，再选「文章」，就是一份现成的爆款文章清单。

搜索： 标题、作者、链接、备注都能搜。输入 @名字 直接搜作者，点卡片上的作者也能只看这个人的收藏。

排序： 收藏时间、发布时间、浏览量、导入时间。

两个快捷键：

另外还能按发布日期范围、是否含外链筛选。超过 3,000 字的普通帖子，卡片上会标「长文」。

五、右键卡片：五个操作

右键卡片，或者点卡片右下角的 ⋯：

  • 打开文章：新标签页打开原帖。
  • 同步文章：访问原帖，只更新这一条的标题和封面。
  • 编辑文章：改标题、加备注。改过的标题以后同步不会被覆盖，备注显示在卡片上，也能被搜到。
  • 下载文章：把正文转成 Markdown 文件下载，含标题、作者、链接、正文、图片链接和备注。
  • 删除文章：从插件里移除，可以立即撤销。

最值钱的是「下载文章」——好文章一键存成 Markdown，直接丢进 Obsidian、Notion 都行。

六、备份·换电脑

管理页点 导出备份，得到一个 JSON 文件。

换电脑、重装之后，点 导入备份 就回来了。

导入只补充缺少的内容，不会覆盖或删除现有数据。

七、隐私：数据只在自己的浏览器里

装这类插件，最该问的是数据去哪了。

  • 插件没有服务器。数据全部保存在当前浏览器本地，不上传，没有统计和广告。
  • 请求只发往 X 自己的网站，不访问其他任何网站。
  • 不保存 Cookie 和密码，不会替你发帖、点赞、关注或修改收藏。
  • 只保存标题、封面链接这类信息，不保存帖子正文。下载 Markdown 时，正文只写进下载的那个文件。

八、常见坑

坑一：升级点了「移除」，收藏全没了。

移除扩展会连同本地资料库一起删掉。升级只需要点扩展卡片上的 重新加载。保险起见，升级前先导出一份备份。

坑二：在插件里删除，X 上的收藏还在。

插件里的删除只动本地，不碰 X。反过来也一样——X 上取消收藏，本地那条还留着。

坑三：同步突然变慢。

X 改版后，插件读不到书签请求，会自动退回滚动页面的兼容模式，能读完，但速度慢。X 改版也可能让同步暂时不可用，等新版本。

坑四：卡片显示「无文字」。

只有图片或视频、没有文字的短帖，本来就没有标题，不是没同步上。

坑五：升级后数据没更新。

最后

entry.title: The $900 Billion Problem Hiding in Anthropic’s IPO
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @blocmates（blocmates.） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

The biggest IPO in history is just around the corner. Anthropic is targeting an IPO between $1 trillion and $1.5 trillion, which is an absolutely insane number.

Just a few hours from now, and we’ll have the exact figure.

Of course, with the official S-1 filings, I’m sure most of you have seen the headline stat of Anthropic reporting a net loss of $104 billion. Although there is more to this number than meets the eye, that’s not what we’re diving into in today’s article.

So you’re probably wondering: $100 billion sounds a whole lot different than $900 billion, so what exactly is this $900 billion problem?

It’s all about future commitments

You see, Anthropic has a dilemma.

Of course, the first part is to actually justify that $1.5 trillion valuation, given that it reported $34 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026. But beyond that is the entire race for AI supremacy.

Anthropic faces competition from the likes of OpenAI, Google, a whole host of open-source models, and the potential unforeseen future competitors/developments that may present themselves in this rapidly changing AI landscape.

To stay ahead of the curve, Anthropic needs to first secure compute over the next 5-10 years to ensure it can continue to innovate and offer the best models.

This has turned Anthropic into more of an infrastructure business rather than just an AI company building models.

Anthropic has reported $895 billion in future commitments with different compute providers, data center infrastructure companies, and cloud service providers.

This $895 billion is split across many different types of deals.

  • Compute spending - This is the standard payment for compute that’s used every day
  • Compute reservation - Anthropic pays to guarantee that a compute provider will provide a minimum amount of compute within a given timeframe
  • Take-or-pay agreement - You agree to pay for a fixed amount of compute regardless of how much you actually use. If you pay for 100 units and only use 70, it doesn’t matter; you still pay the fixed amount
  • Infrastructure lease - signing a fixed multi-year lease with infrastructure like a data center, securing compute for the duration of the lease, regardless of how much use Anthropic gets out of it

Anthropic has a bunch of these deals mixed in its finances with different companies ranging from the likes of Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Amazon’s AWS, which have deals to the tune of $100+ billion each, to the likes of Nscale and Lambda, which have deals in the $40 billion range, to the likes of OnePWR Solutions, which has a commitment for $3.4 billion.

This is what the high-level breakdown looks like.

Forget about the longer-term commitments; given revenue, even the $70 billion due over the next 12 months seems to be a substantial number. Then, over the next 4 years, over half of the $895 billion is expected to be paid.

It’s also explicitly stated in the filings that a lot of these commitment/obligations are expected to be met through future financing.

So yes, the IPO is one way to raise funds, but then it also becomes clear why companies like Anthropic and OpenAI are playing so heavily into the AI doomerism narrative.

Every model update is met with guerrilla marketing along the lines of “We will replace all these jobs,” “You will depend on my AI or die,” “AI will replace humans,” “Every company in the world will be dependent on AI,” “Our AI can hack anything and everything,” “The human race will go extinct if my Claude bot escapes its sandbox,” and so on.

The idea is to bring a national security angle where the entire economy and the people are dependent on companies like Anthropic or OpenAI, so the government is forced to back them rather than “AI models from other enemy nations.”

The government is then forced to become a lender of last resort again and take on the obligations.

There is, of course, no hard evidence to back this theory, but the fact that a 300-page S-1 filing had over 120 pages simply talking about “Risks” does tell a story.

The uncomfortable scenarios

So, with all this being said, what are the actual plausible scenarios under which the $895 billion in commitments could prove to be problematic for Anthropic?

  • AI becomes more efficient

There’s a very plausible near-future scenario in which new technology emerges that makes running AI models significantly cheaper and more efficient.

I mean, it’s already in the works, with companies using laser- and glass-based technologies to make data transmission in data centers much more efficient.

So imagine it typically takes 100 units of compute power to run an AI model. Then, new technology emerges, bringing this requirement down to 20 units.

On the one hand, it’s great for Anthropic, as they can serve more users more cheaply, but on the other hand, many fixed-price deals, like compute reservations or take-or-pay agreements, will prove problematic.

The commitment has already been made, and the money will have to be paid despite the fact that the company is using a negligible amount from the original agreement.

A related issue is that AI is becoming more efficient, which means Anthropic’s competitors are becoming more efficient as well. This makes the landscape more competitive, and those savings get passed on to the users through cheaper APIs etc.

Anthropic then finds itself in a situation where, although it is spending less for each query, it is charging less for each query from a customer base that its competitors are also fighting for. All of this while their commitments still remain substantial.

  • Open-source models continue to get better

Open-source models are already pretty good, but imagine if they start getting significantly better. The problematic part for Anthropic is that in certain scenarios, these models don’t even need to be better than Anthropic; even if they reach a point where they are 90%-95% as good as what Anthropic offers, it becomes easy for companies to make the switch.

A company spending $10 million a year on Claude realizes there’s an open-source alternative that’s almost just as good but can significantly cut down costs by making the switch is likely to make that switch. Why pay a premium if you don’t need to?

Reduced usage means reduced revenue while still having substantial obligations.

Even if Anthropic drives prices down to remain competitive, it will still earn lower revenue per unit of compute and still have those financial commitments looming over its head.

  • Enterprise AI spending slows down

Currently, only 20% of Anthropic’s revenue comes from subscriptions, and the remaining 80% comes from enterprise AI; that means companies pay based on how much they actually use Claude.

So it’s very different from SaaS businesses that have the security of multi-year fixed subscription contracts with major companies.

Anthropic needs to remain at the top of its game and continue to be better than its competitors to ensure that Enterprise AI spending doesn’t slow down, thereby hampering future revenue and increasing losses with its fixed commitments.

  • Regulatory troubles

Another issue is that regulators don’t end up favouring these AI companies.

With the recent Democratic win in the midterms, there’s a lot of chat around regulators shutting down data center/infrasturtucre projects and maybe even being less favourable in terms of general regulation for these AI companies.

While it may seem like a concern now, I’m willing to bet that this is simply a campaign promise unlikely to be followed through on.

After some time, I believe that, when it comes down to it, regulators will favor these AI companies in certain situations and do it in a way that the public is less privy to the details. And in the worst-case scenario, I do believe there will be some semblance of a government bailout.

So not a major issue, but one to think about.

The flip side: Why Anthropic might actually be right

There are always two sides to every story, and as much as we like to nitpick the various issues with these companies, they also have some of the smartest minds in the world working there, so there’s surely a reason behind some of these moves.

Let’s look at why Anthropic might have made these obligations.

  • AI demand grows faster than infrastructure supply

As an AI company, the baseline expectation is that demand for AI is going to continually grow. One of the main reasons is that they are probably working on things behind the scenes that we have no idea about, and hence they’ve taken the bets that they have.

But outside of the unknown, it’s a very real possibility that AI agents get deeply entrenched into every aspect of every business. This means the demand will significantly outweigh the compute supply.

Imagine millions of companies running hundreds of agents each for every aspect of their business, running queries and calls every second of every day. That’s a lot of demand. Add to that the possibility of even more powerful products in the near future, and things start to look good.

  • Compute is a competitive moat

Compute is quickly becoming the most important commodity in the world. Not securing enough compute as one of the biggest players in the AI space could prove to be a HUGE risk.

With so many competitors vying for the same resource, Anthropic is in a situation where you’d rather be safe than sorry. You’d rather have extra compute and not need it than have less compute and desperately need it.

It’s imperative for them to stay at the top of the game.

  • Long-term infrastructure could be cheaper

Anthropic stated in its filing that moving towards dedicated infrastructure, which is a big element of these future obligation deals, could actually prove to be cheaper.

It gives them access to more cost-effective compute because short-term compute deals can be expensive. If you own the infrastructure and can rely on it for compute whenever needed, the investment pays for itself over time, depending on how much the demand for AI actually grows.

Concluding thoughts

At the end of it, the problems come down to a bunch of “what ifs.”

The AI landscape, just like any other internet-native sector, is evolving rapidly. New technology emerges every other week, bringing in new challenges and situations.

Currently, it seems that Anthropic may have more problems than positives, especially given the outlandish valuation.

From here on out, it’s a game of observing, analyzing, and reacting to whether Anthropic makes sense after its IPO, whether the ridiculous burn rate can be justified, and how the regulators react.

entry.title: 我用 ChatGPT 做了一款微信小游戏
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @momo_peggy（夏林果的出海日记） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

一个季度流水超过1000万元，这样的微信小游戏，已经有300多款。

这是2026年5月微信小游戏开发者大会公布的过去一年数据。同场公布的还有：80多款小游戏，日活跃用户超过100万。

大家都说小游戏已经卷到天际了，但是看到这些数字，我仍然想知道：这门生意，个人借助 AI 到底有没有机会做？

我自己在一家手游公司上班，公司做的是一款知名IP的MMO手游，其中一个渠道就是小游戏的版本，所以我深知要做一款重度游戏，仍然还是需要大量人力物力 去支撑。

可是如果是轻度游戏呢，不是SLG,MMO,MOBA，而是点点点 ，刷刷刷呢？

带着疑问，我撸起袖子说干就干，全程只用了Chatgpt，做了一款轻松解谜类游戏 - 《谜题必须解开》

今天我就聊聊 ，我是怎么从0开始到做完第一个版本。

1. 一个人做游戏，AI 能帮到什么程度

公司做游戏分以下的职位，制作人、策划、程序开发、美术、测试

原来程序开发门槛最高，现在变成人人皆是天才程序员了

然后现在策划变成了香饽饽 ，因为我做这个游戏的过程中，觉得AI 最代替不了的就是顺畅的玩法和合适的点子

作为程序员，我都没有写一行代码，全程中文PUA
美术也是让Chatgpt直接出图

只有游戏要怎么进行，系统要怎么闭环，哪里体验不友好，只需要我自己动脑思考的

所以AI确实很强大，已经帮你做 你以前做不了的事情了，但是要想有核心竞争力，还是得想象力丰富的人类的小脑瓜

2. 选哪个游戏引擎？

那做游戏常用的几个引擎如下：

  • | 引擎 | 主要区别 | 我会在什么情况下考虑 |
  • | —————– | ——————————————————- | —————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————- |
  • | Cocos Creator | 可以在编辑器里搭场景，官方提供微信小游戏打包流程。 | 目标明确是微信，想做找物、消除、休闲闯关这类游戏，可以优先研究它的发布流程。官方说明 |
  • | Unity／团结引擎 | 有完整的 2D、3D 制作工具，覆盖动画、物理等功能。团结是 Unity 中国版，有自己的微信小游戏部署方案。 | 已有 Unity 基础，或者准备做需要较多 3D 场景和角色动画的游戏，可以列入候选；先确认所用版本对应的发布路径。引擎介绍、微信部署 |
  • | Godot | 免费开源，不收引擎版税；支持 2D、3D，可以导出桌面、手机和网页游戏。 | 想做独立游戏，也愿意学一点脚本，希望制作工具和项目都能自己掌握。官方介绍 |
  • | GDevelop | 用可视化事件组织玩法，例如点中物品后加分，也提供 AI 辅助制作。 | 暂时不想从编程入门，想先把一个小玩法做出来、发个链接给朋友试试。引擎介绍、发布方式 |

可以先按照自己的游戏喜好来做，我基本什么类型的游戏都喜欢玩，只是尤其喜欢解谜类的，所以我想先做2D解谜类的游戏，

基于这个情况， 我选择了微信开发者工具 😂 ，对 ，没有用任何游戏引擎，主要是我觉得，这个小游戏用不上牛刀

当然，这些引擎，你不需要会，你只要知道就行，然后根据你想做的游戏类型问AI 适合用哪个引擎，让他推荐就行，反正都是它干货。

3. 第一个关卡

选好引擎了，开始做我的第一关卡

当然我这个脑子，重新想出一个全新的游戏是不可能的
肯定要站在巨人的肩膀上啊

所以我找了一款我觉得不错的游戏
然后体验后，决定要复刻它一关打个样，把流程跑一下

所以 我基于体验的结果后，跟AI简单的说了下 我的整个体验过程
我希望做一个从画面中找出所有人物这样一个简单的玩法
大部分人是很轻易能找到 但是有少数几个需要动脑看看 查一查才能找到

然后让它给我出了一个简易的测试玩法 如下图

因为是测试玩法，就真的给我出的非常简陋
但是 大体是符合我的想法的

所以当这个测试玩法通过后，我就让它基于此 ，加上风格开始出资源和写代码。最终效果如下：

当然这是玩之前的效果 ，如果你感兴趣，可以扫标题图的小程序码来体验下，我敢说98%的人不靠提示找不到所有人。

好了，上面都说了些我开始做游戏的历程，下面给一些真正可以系统化，我当时最先建立项目的提示词

4. 工作流的改变

我就这样一关一关的制作，前面两个关卡做了好几天，因为总是没有达到我想要的效果，而且也是刚开始制作，资源分层和资源生成顺序都是想一出是一出
风格也是换了又换

然后发现 原来眼中的 那么简单的游戏用AI复现做起来也是挺费劲的

AI的精细度和仔细度都很差，需要人为定点去纠正
还总愿意糊弄你，交出一个非常粗劣的版本交差

但是怎么提高效率和质量呢

第一有些事情 就是做着做着发现怎么做才效果好，也就是经验

比如生成资源，我改了好几个版本，开始是整图出，再分别对互动物件进行抠图，但是抠图的效果差强人意，又变成全部互动物件单独出，又遇到了 单独出的组合在一起又有非常强烈的拼凑感，不和谐不统一

然后我反反复复在这中间来回拉扯

最后咋解决的呢
就是还是先出带有逻辑的整图，然后专门做了一个技能来对互动物件做分层，风格尽量不要那么写实
然后就是不断的修改 😂

再看看做这个新关卡的测试demo 只测试玩法 不生成资源

还是简陋至极，但是我开始做的时候 新鲜感还十足
后来，当我一周才做出两个关卡的时候
我就开始打起邪修的主意

5. 开始邪修

因为游戏性质的原因，我需要大量的关卡来支撑游戏内容，而且我所参考的成熟游戏里面大概有1300多关 ，所以我希望我推出的首个版本最少包含30个关卡内容，然后每个关卡内容又要有所不同，不断的要给与玩家新的新鲜感，

但是我之前的制作方法不但慢，还总偷懒，放假的时候总想着玩，做10关都不知道要搞到猴年马月

然后，我想了一个招，我把玩别的游戏的一个关卡的全程录下来，然后 直接发给chatgpt然后跟他说就按照视频的内容，大致换个风格 ，玩法加几个减几个，直接给我出一个可玩关卡。

本着试试看的想法，结果意外的结果不错，基本很快就搭出一个框子 ，然后基于框架，我就源源不断的出现新的想法和意见，还可以同时出多个关卡，我需要做的就是不断的给意见和修改内容。

就这样，一下干到50关，改的昏天暗地的
天天PUA chatgpt 并把从视频做成关卡也搞成skill
终于感觉自己的游戏有一丁点看头了

最后 ，我觉得做游戏主要就两个优化

截图给AI说 ，这个优化一下，那个优化一下😂 没错就这两个

不是开玩笑，其实是想说好游戏是慢慢改出来的，以我的工作经验来说，成熟游戏都是要长期打磨出来的，而不是一下子设计出来的

6. 要相信自己

作为游戏程序员，我天天的工作都是在大型游戏里添加玩法系统、优化、服务器功能和迭代

但是我开始做游戏还是怀疑自己的
但是我又非常喜欢玩游戏

所以why not
带着疑虑和困惑开始了

我以为我没啥想法，脑袋空空，但是有些东西自然而然的就跳出来
很多问号自动冒出

所以 ，把这些问题解决，把执行力拉满
也许命运的齿轮开始转动了呢

虽然游戏我还不是很满意，但是一个雏形已经出来了
我现在有时候工作或者在哪个环境下的时候都会自动想到这个场景可以放进来做成关卡
这可能就是真的热爱吧

如果你也喜欢玩游戏，要不要看看这款一个普通人用AI做出来的游戏是啥样的

而且最重要的是做出这样的游戏，到底能不能赚到钱？我会持续更新后续

我是宋宋，很感谢你看完我写的内容 X：@songsong

entry.title: 不用海外卡，微信就能开 Claude 会员：自己的号直充、合租、4 折 Claude Code，一篇讲清
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @TuyetloanP81840（Miller） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

想用 Claude，却被海外卡、扣款失败、收不到验证码挡在门外的，这篇建议直接收藏。

Fable 5.2 刚上线，想第一时间用上 Claude 的人，第一道坎还是付款。

我自己做 AI 短剧，剧本、分镜基本都交给 Claude。带冲刺班这几期，学员问得最多的也不是提示词，而是这几句：

  • 虚拟卡又被拒了
  • 第一个月能扣，第二个月扣款失败
  • 账单地址到底填哪
  • 注册 Claude 收不到验证码

我现在给学员的统一答案是 WildAI（bewild.ai）：已经服务超过 20 万用户，微信、支付宝直接付，不用海外卡，也不用折腾虚拟卡。

Claude、ChatGPT、Gemini 订阅，Codex 充值，Claude Code 和开发者 API，连注册要用的接码，一个站全有。

它最实在的地方，是按你的情况拆成了四条路，对号入座就行。

① 有自己的号：微信直充，会员开在你自己账号上

这是我最推荐的一条，也是它的主业。

这条不是中转：会员直接开在你自己的官方账号上，聊天记录、Project、攒下来的提示词全在自己号里，不会因为换号丢掉。

页面上的起步价：

  • Claude Pro / Max / Ultra：$25.99/月起
  • ChatGPT Go / Plus / Pro：$9.99/月起
  • Gemini Pro / Ultra：$9.45/月起
  • Claude API：$25.99 起
  • Codex Credit：$24.99 起

流程很简单：邮箱登录 → 选套餐 → 按提示上传账号授权信息 → 微信或支付宝付款，系统自动完成升级。第一次用，页面上有视频教程，跟着走一遍就行。

选档建议：刚入门写剧本、拆分镜，Claude Pro 就够；天天用 Claude Code 跑长任务、经常顶到额度，再上 Max。先开一个月，摸清自己的用量再加时长。

② 不想用官方账号：Claude Code / Codex 4 折，开发者 API 8 折

不想注册、也不想管账号的，走这条：

  • Claude Code / Codex： 无需账户，按量或订阅，页面标 4 折。
  • 开发者 API： 按量计费，OpenAI、Claude、Gemini 都有，页面标 8 折。

拿刚出的 Fable 5.2 算一笔：官方 API 价是每百万 tokens 输入 $8、输出 $40，按 8 折就是 $6.4 和 $32。

月卡里的 tokens 30 天内随便分配，今天没用完明天接着用，到期清零。新用户还能买一次单日体验。

这条要说清楚：它本质是平台中转。它家 FAQ 写得很直白，是从自己购买的企业版 Claude Code / Codex 账户里中转出来的 API。好处是便宜、不用外卡、不用自己的号；代价是请求经过平台，用的不是你自己的官方账号。按需求选。

想要单独入口的，它家还有 0011（https://3366.ai/），专做 Claude Code 和 Codex 编程接入，带图形界面客户端 0011 Code，内置 Claude Code 和 Codex 引擎，不用装命令行。

原理是把一批已付费账号封装成一个镜像站，大家共享额度，你不需要官方账号。对话是隔离的，别人看不到你的记录。

限制页面上也写了：只能网页端用，App 登不上，每次使用随机分配账号。适合预算有限、主要在网页上聊天写东西的人。

合租也有独立站 2233（https://2233.ai/）：ChatGPT Plus、Claude Pro、Gemini Pro 都有，$7.99/月起，买完直接开聊，不用自己订官方账号。

④ 卡在注册这一步：短信验证和一次性号码

很多人不是付不了款，是连号都注册不下来，验证码死活收不到。

  • 短信验证服务： 长期有效的独享号码，Codex / Claude 注册专用。

页面写着可以用于注册 Codex、Claude、Google、X 等产品。

客服和退款，口径摆在明面上

7×12 小时在线客服，网页右下角就有「联络客服」入口，买之前、买之后都能问。

  • 订阅成功后失效： 优先帮你修复；修不好，按剩余有效期折算退款。

唯一要看清的边界

最后三条，我放在明面上讲：

第一，直充要上传账号授权信息。 也就是把你账号的登录授权临时交给平台去完成升级。介意这一点的，走合租或 API。

entry.title: 自媒体创作不完全指南：如何打造数字人 IP「新手极度友好」
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @leaf_sanren（Leaf Yeah!） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

想做自媒体，又不想自己露脸？很简单，今天就教你们用手机做一个自己的数字人 IP，新手极度友好！！

Hello，上一篇讲了怎么快速起号，不少朋友问我：复刻爆款确实能拿到第一波播放，但账号想长期做下去，总得有个固定的人设吧？

上篇帖子👇🏻

确实，观众记住的是一个人，而不是某一条视频。

说实话，其实我挺想做口播的。但我比较纠结😖，就是自己不想出镜。而且拍摄好麻烦，还得看提词器，总之我不喜欢😄

另，现在做视频的人越来越多，如果没有一个固定的 IP 让别人认识你，其实会少点信任感，流量上也会有点吃亏。

我身边不少人也有同样的情况：

  • **个人自媒体起号，**想稳定更新，但自己不想露脸，平时也不一定抽得出时间拍。
  • **商家做矩阵号，**老板号讲行业选品，门店号回答用户的问题。几个号都要持续更新，光是协调人员、场地和拍摄，就要花不少精力。

所以，想要出片快、成本低，又不用自己出镜，数字人就是当下最好的选择。给账号一个出镜角色，把形象和声音固定下来，以后换个选题，就可以接着用。

只是传统做法比较折腾，分开做的话，素材得在几个工具之间来回倒腾。剪完发现念错一句，重录完还得回头把嘴型和字幕重新对一遍。

不过我今天找到一个好方法，用手机就能很快做出一条数字人口播

🔥废话不多说，直接上干货。

一、常规做法

数字人本质上就是让一个固定的形象替代真人开口讲内容

大致以下5个步骤：

  1. 定人设：想清楚给谁讲、讲什么、用什么语气。建议把参考图、音色和样本文案存进固定文件夹，后续直接调用；
  2. 准备形象：真人视频定制需要在光线均匀的环境下，一镜到底录几分钟；原创虚拟形象用一张正面清晰照片即可。全身图适合介绍展示，正面口播建议挑面部更清楚的近景；
  3. 写稿与配音：口播稿多用短句，写完自己读一遍，顺口才行；挑选贴合角色的音色，圈出专有名词重点听发音；
  4. 生成口播与检查口型：人像加音频驱动嘴型。第一次建议拿一句短句试跑，看嘴型跟不跟得上、停顿表情是否自然、前后五官是否稳定；
  5. 剪辑与包装：把原片导入剪映去停顿、加字幕花字、在关键处补插图空镜、配背景乐。

⚠️传统做法最大的成本不是生成，而是素材要在四五个工具间来回导出导入；最怕的是改了一处就牵连整条剪辑轴，全盘推倒重来。

二、手机实操

上个月我在电脑上用 Renoise 做过一条万圣节换装视频👇🏻

这次使用的是 👉🏻 手机版 Renoise App，还是用我的 专属IP 来出镜

APP功能演示如下

1.新建项目

打开 App，新建一个项目，直接说需求就行，建议用语音输入法，因为打字太累🤣

我是这么说的：

我想用数字人口播技能做一条视频。主播给做自媒体的新手讲一些经验，语气像朋友聊天。前半段讲传统做数字人要经过哪些步骤，后半段讲怎么在手机上用 Renoise 去做。

它会先复述一遍理解，再问主播用谁的形象

2. 选出镜画面

上传IP照片，它会先出两张出镜画面给你挑，我选了客厅沙发这张。生成之前它会先告诉你要花多少积分，确认了才开始做。

3. 生成口播

稿子它会先写一版，我让它按这篇文章改了改。改好以后自己念一遍，书面词换成平时说话的样子。

确认后，用 App 里现成的 「数字人口播」 技能生成口播，照片加稿子，她就像真人博主一样开口讲了。

4. 剪辑成片

口播做好了，就交给 「口播剪辑」 技能。让它把多余的停顿剪掉，加上字幕，讲到具体操作的地方就补一段录屏。

5. 局部微调

等它剪出一版，先看一遍。哪儿不满意，就在成片上点一下，跟它说这一段想怎么改。改好了直接下载。

🔥完整操作演示如下

三、技能推荐🔥

App 里面其实内置了很多现成的技能（Skill），相当于把成熟的视频流水线打包好了，直接调用能少走很多弯路。

目前做数字人口播，用上面这两个组合就足够了：

  • 「数字人口播」：负责根据照片和稿子生成稳定开口说话的画面；
  • 「口播剪辑」：负责自动切除空白气口、对齐字幕，并把素材画面顺畅剪进去。

除此之外，它里面还有几个可玩性非常强的技能，强烈推荐大家去试：

  1. 「爆款复刻」（🔥🔥强烈推荐）： 这个功能极度实用。平时刷到小红书、B站、X 或 TikTok 上的爆款视频，直接把链接复制发给它，它能保留原片的爆款结构、镜头语言和剪辑节奏，把里面的主角、台词和素材换成你自己的，起号和批量测素材非常高效；
  2. 「Vox 风格拼贴解说片」： 复古报纸拼贴质感、历史照片、印章红线，自带纪录片的高级网感。特别适合拿来做深度科普、行业解析、热点话题或人物故事；
  3. 「萌宠 3D 动画片」&「低多边形 3D 冷知识」： 把故事或冷知识写给它，就能生成 3D 动画短片。适合做不露脸的治愈宠物号或者趣味科普号。

四、使用技巧

  1. 先聊清楚再生成：聊想法、改脚本方案完全不扣积分，只有确认生成画面和剪辑时才计费。方向拿不准时多跟它聊几轮，不用心疼积分；
  2. 日常口播选 Wan 3.0：常规知识口播用 Wan 3.0 表现足够稳定，而且消耗积分明显更低，适合高频日更；
  3. 追求质感用 Seedance 2.5，先出 480P 样片：先用低清样片看动作和构图，方向确认无误后再出高清，避免前期调试浪费积分；
  4. 多端随时同步：手机、电脑无缝衔接

五、最后

做自媒体，核心始终是你的选题和认知，出不出镜只是一种表达方式。

数字人做的，就是把拍摄、对口型、剪辑这些繁琐的重复劳动接过去，让你把精力留给真正重要的内容本身。

如果你也一直卡在「不想露脸」这一步，不妨先给自己做一个数字人，从第一条口播开始。

entry.title: 没有海外股票账户，如何用数字钱包参与新股认购？
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @0xshimei（0x小师妹） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

国内用户想玩美股、黄金之类的产品，要跨两个门槛。第一道是账户：海外券商要开户、等审核。第二道是钱：美元得先换汇，换完两边各压一笔，黄金这边缺钱的时候，那边明明有余额，却用不上。

有一类做法就是冲着这两道门来的：把黄金、白银、外汇、纳指这些传统市场，做成用稳定币结算的链上合约。稳定币就是锚定美元的数字货币，开仓前要先押进去的那笔钱叫保证金。买卖的是价格涨跌，平仓时按价差结算，不交割实物金条，所以不用开券商户、不用换汇，同一笔钱在不同品种之间都能用。它是杠杆合约，不是买一块金子放着。

有个平台叫@XStableAI。背后有 YZi Labs（前身是币安旗下的投资机构）等十几家机构投资，项目得到过 Solana 基金会的孵化支持。黄金、白银、欧元、英镑、纳指 100 和 BTC、ETH 都在同一张交易页里。

1. 门槛有多低？

用钱包连接，或者直接用谷歌账号登录，不用实名开户。打开 https://www.xstable.ai/trade?ref=UEG8BK就能进，通过邀请链接注册的用户，交易手续费有 10% 折扣。入金支持USDT或者USD1，最低支持1美元起，门槛非常低；同时还支持 Solana、Sui、BNB Chain 和 Monad 几条链。

充值分两种：快速存款走的是当前钱包所在的网络；正常存款可以选币种和网络，每次给一个专属充值地址，再打开就换新的。另外平台有模拟交易账户，新手可以先在上面把下单、设止盈止损这套练熟，再放真钱。

我当时登录用的是 Solana 钱包，手里的 USDT 是 BSC链的，就直接转到 BNB Chain 的充值地址。平台很快把钱归集到交易账户，余额记在 Solana 这一侧。第一次碰到挺意外：钱是从 BNB Chain 转的，但是依然可以存在SOL钱包，省去了传统钱包网络不同做交易前还要跨链的步骤

2. Xstable相比其它平台的优势在哪

最直观的一条是杠杆，最高 500 倍，下单区可以选 20、50、100、200、500 倍。拿当时盘面上的黄金来算，约 4100 美元的仓位，500 倍下占用的保证金只要 8 美元出头，小资金也能碰黄金，对高风险投资爱好者的我来说，简直是交易天堂

另外Xstable还留了程序化交易的接口。平台已经上线 API、WebSocket 和 AI Agent 接入，会用AI的人可以把自己的策略接上去，让它自动做交易。

3. 提现门槛

提款最低 1 美元是我比较意外的，因为尝试过很多网页版交易平台，大多都会卡提现，正常都要10U起步，所以这个平台对小资金挺友好的，看得出不是靠抬高提现门槛把人留下。试了下提现速度，我从平台提回自己钱包，大约 30 秒到账。

4. 交易积分怎么算，亏了也有补贴？

交易会记 CP，也就是平台的贡献积分。不同品种的基础积分不一样：黄金、白银按手数算，BTC、ETH 按成交额算。平台每期拿出收入的 20%，按各人的 CP 权重分，本期拿到的 CP 按 2 倍权重算。

平仓亏了，符合条件的单子还会按亏损占保证金的比例多补 CP：亏得不到 10% 补 20%，亏到 60% 以上最高补 100%。持仓不足 5 分钟的单子不算，同一个人在两个方向上对冲刷量也不算。另外每过一期，积分的换算比例会降 2%，最低降到 50%，所以越早交易，同样的量拿到的积分越多。

第一期累计付满 10 美元手续费，可以拿到「创始股东」身份，带创始人徽章会获得终身分红资格；如果本来就要交易，这就是妥妥的早期玩家才有的福利。

5. 哪些还没落地？

现金分红的首次发放时间、积分盲盒、代币空投凭证，目前都标着待公布；跟单交易、铂金和钯金合约、直接用银行卡出入金，也还在计划中。目前能用的，就是上面走过的这一套。

适合想在原来的钱包里加做黄金、纳指，又不想另开账户、换汇的人，上面这套从入金到提现都能照着走一遍。
